ramayana-6-44-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-15.translation: Knowing himself without a weapon, full of anger, the bull among monkeys quickly tore up a mountain.
ramayana-6-44-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-16.translation: Holding that great rock in one hand, mighty Hanuman gave a great roar and whirled it.
ramayana-6-44-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-17.translation: Then he rushed at Akampana, lord of demons, as Indra rushed at Namuchi in battle with the thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-44-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-18.translation: Seeing the raised mountain peak, Akampana shattered it from afar with great crescent arrows.
ramayana-6-44-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-44-19.translation: Seeing the mountain top split by the demon's arrows in the sky and fallen scattered, Hanuman grew wild with anger.
ramayana-6-44-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-20.translation: Full of rage and pride, the monkey went to an ashvakarna tree and quickly tore it up, tall as a great mountain.
ramayana-6-44-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-21.translation: Holding that great-trunked ashvakarna, the splendid one, laughing with great joy, whirled it in battle.
ramayana-6-44-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-22.translation: Running with great speed, breaking trees by force, very angry Hanuman split the earth with his feet.
ramayana-6-44-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-23.translation: Wise Hanuman struck down elephants with their riders, chariots with their warriors, and demons on foot.
ramayana-6-44-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-44-24.translation: Seeing Hanuman angry in battle like Death, taker of lives, the demons fled.
ramayana-6-44-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-25.translation: Seeing him coming, angry, frightening the demons, heroic Akampana grew angry and roared.
ramayana-6-44-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-26.translation: Akampana pierced mighty Hanuman with fourteen sharp arrows.
ramayana-6-44-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-44-27.translation: Pierced by many showers of arrows, heroic Hanuman looked like a mountain covered with growing trees.
ramayana-6-44-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-28.translation: Then tearing up another tree with unmatched speed, he quickly struck Akampana, lord of demons, on the head.
ramayana-6-44-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-44-29.translation: Struck by that tree by the angry great monkey lord, the demon fell and died.
ramayana-6-44-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-44-30.translation: Seeing Akampana, lord of demons, struck down on the ground, all the demons were shaken like trees in an earthquake.
ramayana-6-44-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-31.translation: Throwing away their weapons, all the defeated demons ran to Lanka in fear, chased by the monkeys.
ramayana-6-44-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-32.translation: Hair loose, panicked, pride broken, defeated, their limbs streaming with sweat, gasping, they fled.
ramayana-6-44-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-33.translation: Crushing each other they entered the city in fear, confused, looking back again and again.
ramayana-6-44-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-34.translation: When the demons had gone into Lanka, all the mighty monkeys gathered and honoured Hanuman.
ramayana-6-44-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-35.translation: Joyful, Hanuman, full of goodness, honoured all those monkeys in return, as each deserved, kindly.
ramayana-6-44-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all. Hanuman returns honour to his friends.

ramayana-6-44-36.translation: The victorious monkeys roared with all their might.
ramayana-6-44-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-37.translation: The great monkey, son of the Wind, gained a hero's glory by meeting and killing the demons and the great fearsome foe, as Vishnu did with Bali at the army's front.
ramayana-6-44-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-44-38.translation: Then the hosts of gods honoured the monkey, and so did Rama himself, mighty Lakshmana, the monkeys led by Sugriva, and mighty Vibhishana.
ramayana-6-44-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 44: Hanuman defeats Akampana and is honoured by all.

ramayana-6-45-1.translation: Hearing of Akampana's death, the lord of demons, angry and somewhat downcast, looked at his ministers.
ramayana-6-45-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-2.translation: After thinking a moment and talking with his ministers, he went round the city of Lanka to inspect all the posts.
ramayana-6-45-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-3.translation: He saw the city of Lanka guarded by hosts of demons, surrounded by many posts, garlanded with flags and banners.
ramayana-6-45-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-4.translation: Seeing the city blockaded, Ravana, lord of demons, angrily said at the right moment to Prahasta, skilled in war:
ramayana-6-45-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-5.translation: "For the city, besieged and suddenly pressed, I see no release other than battle, master of war."
ramayana-6-45-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-6.translation: "Only I, Kumbhakarna, you my commander, Indrajit or Nikumbha could carry such a burden."
ramayana-6-45-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-7.translation: "So quickly take a force from here and march out for victory to where all the forest-dwellers are."
ramayana-6-45-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-8.translation: "As soon as you march out, the fickle monkey army will surely flee on hearing the roar of the demon lords."
ramayana-6-45-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army. Ravana underestimates the monkeys again.

ramayana-6-45-9.translation: "Monkeys are fickle, undisciplined and restless; they will not bear your roar, as elephants cannot bear a lion's roar."
ramayana-6-45-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-10.translation: "When that army has fled, Rama with Saumitri, helpless and without support, will fall into Prahasta's power."
ramayana-6-45-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-11.translation: "Good fortune is uncertain in danger, not made certain here. Whether for or against, tell me what you think best for us."
ramayana-6-45-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-12.translation: Told this by Ravana, Prahasta the commander said to the demon king, as Ushanas speaks to the asura king:
ramayana-6-45-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-13.translation: "King, we have discussed this before with wise ministers, and there was disagreement among us after we looked at each other's views."
ramayana-6-45-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-14.translation: "I decided that the good lay in returning Sita; if she was not returned, we saw war, just as it has come."
ramayana-6-45-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army. Prahasta also once advised returning Sita.

ramayana-6-45-15.translation: "Always honoured by you with gifts, respect and many kind words in time, what would I not do to please you?"
ramayana-6-45-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-16.translation: "I do not guard my life, my sons, wife or wealth. See me offer my life in battle for you."
ramayana-6-45-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-17.translation: Having said this to his master Ravana, the commander said: "Bring me quickly a great army of demons."
ramayana-6-45-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-18.translation: "Today let the birds feed on those forest-dwellers struck on the battlefield by my thunderbolt-swift arrows."
ramayana-6-45-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army. A grim boast before battle.

ramayana-6-45-19.translation: Told this by Prahasta, the army chiefs hurried and made the army ready in that demon palace.
ramayana-6-45-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-20.translation: In a moment Lanka was crowded with those demon heroes with many sharp weapons, as with elephants.
ramayana-6-45-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-21.translation: As they fed the sacred fire and bowed to Brahmins, a fragrant wind blew carrying the scent of ghee.
ramayana-6-45-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-22.translation: The demons, ready for battle and thrilled, took and wore garlands of many shapes, charged with mantras.
ramayana-6-45-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-23.translation: With bows and armour, the demons leapt up swiftly and, seeing King Ravana, gathered round Prahasta.
ramayana-6-45-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-24.translation: Then, taking leave of the king and beating a fearsome drum, Prahasta mounted a divine chariot made ready.
ramayana-6-45-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-25.translation: It was yoked with very swift horses, well driven, roaring like a great cloud, shining like the moon and sun.
ramayana-6-45-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-26.translation: Hard to assail, with a serpent banner, good guard rails and fittings, with a golden net, it seemed to smile with splendour.
ramayana-6-45-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-27.translation: Mounting that chariot, with Ravana's command, he quickly went out of Lanka surrounded by a great army.
ramayana-6-45-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-28.translation: Then as the commander set out, the boom of kettledrums like thunder and the sound of conches were heard.
ramayana-6-45-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Ravana sends his commander Prahasta, who marches out with a great army.

ramayana-6-45-29.translation: Fearsome, huge demons went ahead of Prahasta, roaring terrible cries.
ramayana-6-45-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

ramayana-6-45-30.translation: He went out by the eastern gate in a very fierce formation, surrounded by a great army like a herd of elephants.
ramayana-6-45-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

ramayana-6-45-31.translation: Surrounded by that army vast as the ocean, Prahasta went out quickly, angry, like Death at the end of time.
ramayana-6-45-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

keywords.meaning: Death at the end of time

ramayana-6-45-32.translation: At the noise of his march and the demons' roars, all the creatures in Lanka cried out with strange voices.
ramayana-6-45-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near.

ramayana-6-45-33.translation: Flesh-eating birds flew into the cloudless sky and circled his chariot to the left.
ramayana-6-45-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near.

ramayana-6-45-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near.

ramayana-6-45-35.translation: A meteor fell from the sky, a harsh wind blew, and the planets, clashing with each other, did not shine.
ramayana-6-45-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near.

ramayana-6-45-36.translation: Blood rained down on those going ahead of him, and a vulture settled on his banner top facing south.
ramayana-6-45-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near. South is the direction of Yama, god of death.

ramayana-6-45-37.translation: As he plunged into battle, the whip fell again and again from the hand of his charioteer.
ramayana-6-45-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near.

ramayana-6-45-38.translation: The rare bright glory he had as he set out vanished in a moment, and his horses stumbled on level ground.
ramayana-6-45-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens. Omens like these show that disaster is near.

ramayana-6-45-39.translation: As Prahasta, famous for strength and courage, came out, the monkey army with many weapons advanced against him.
ramayana-6-45-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

ramayana-6-45-40.translation: Then a wild shout arose from the monkeys, tearing up trees and grabbing heavy rocks.
ramayana-6-45-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

ramayana-6-45-41.translation: Both armies, of demons and forest-dwellers, were thrilled; the great noise of those swift, able fighters, eager to kill each other and challenging each other, was heard.
ramayana-6-45-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

ramayana-6-45-42.translation: Then foolish Prahasta advanced on the monkey king's army for victory, and entered that swelling host like a moth that wants to die entering fire.
ramayana-6-45-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 45: Prahasta marches out amid evil omens.

ramayana-6-46-1.translation: Then, seeing Prahasta come out, fearsome, of fearsome valour, roaring, huge, surrounded by demons...
ramayana-6-46-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-2.translation: ...the great army of strong monkeys saw him and, very angry, roared at Prahasta.
ramayana-6-46-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-3.translation: Swords, spears, darts, arrows, tridents, clubs, maces, bars, lances and many axes...
ramayana-6-46-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-4.translation: ...and bright bows held by the demons, eager for victory, shone as they rushed at the monkeys.
ramayana-6-46-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-5.translation: The bull-like monkeys, eager to fight, took up flowering trees and great long rocks.
ramayana-6-46-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-6.translation: As they met, a very great battle arose, with many raining showers of stones and showers of arrows.
ramayana-6-46-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-7.translation: Many demons in battle struck down many monkey leaders, and many monkeys struck down many demons.
ramayana-6-46-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-8.translation: Some were struck by tridents, some by great weapons, some by bars, some cut by axes.
ramayana-6-46-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-9.translation: Some fell breathless to the ground, some wounded by streams of arrows.
ramayana-6-46-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-10.translation: Some fell on the ground struck by swords; monkeys were wounded by demons' tridents.
ramayana-6-46-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-11.translation: Hosts of demons too were crushed on the ground all around by angry monkeys with trees and mountain peaks.
ramayana-6-46-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-12.translation: Struck hard by hands with palms like thunderbolts and by fists, demons were badly hurt.
ramayana-6-46-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-13.translation: Cries of pain and lion roars made a wild noise of monkeys and demons in battle.
ramayana-6-46-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-14.translation: Angry monkeys and demons, following the path of heroes, eyes rolling, fierce, did their deeds without fear.
ramayana-6-46-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-15.translation: Narantaka, Kumbhahanu, Mahanada and Samunnata, Prahasta's companions, all struck the forest-dwellers.
ramayana-6-46-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-16.translation: As they rushed on quickly, striking monkeys, Dvivida struck down one of them, Narantaka, with a mountain peak.
ramayana-6-46-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-17.translation: The quick-handed monkey Durmukha tore up a great tree and struck down the demon Samunnata.
ramayana-6-46-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-18.translation: Very angry, mighty Jambavan took a huge rock and brought it down on Mahanada's chest.
ramayana-6-46-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-19.translation: Then mighty Kumbhahanu met Tara and, struck on the head by a tree, the demon gave up his life.
ramayana-6-46-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-20.translation: Unable to bear this, Prahasta, in his chariot, bow in hand, made a dreadful slaughter of the forest-dwellers.
ramayana-6-46-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-21.translation: Both armies swirled like a whirlpool, with a noise like the stirred, boundless ocean.
ramayana-6-46-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-22.translation: With a great flood of arrows, angry Prahasta, skilled in war, tormented the monkeys in the great battle.
ramayana-6-46-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-23.translation: The ground became heaped with the fallen of both sides, as if with fallen hills.
ramayana-6-46-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-24.translation: The red-stained ground looked like a field covered in red palasha flowers in spring.
ramayana-6-46-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. The epic pictures the battlefield as a grim river; the app keeps the image brief.

ramayana-6-46-25.translation: The battlefield became like a river flowing toward Yama's sea, its banks of fallen heroes and broken weapons.
ramayana-6-46-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. The epic pictures the battlefield as a grim river; the app keeps the image brief.

ramayana-6-46-26.translation: Its mud and weeds were the dreadful leavings of battle.
ramayana-6-46-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. The epic pictures the battlefield as a grim river; the app keeps the image brief.

ramayana-6-46-27.translation: It was crowded with vultures and herons, flecked with foam, and full of groans.
ramayana-6-46-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. The epic pictures the battlefield as a grim river; the app keeps the image brief.

ramayana-6-46-28.translation: That river of battle, hard for cowards to cross, was like a river after the rains, visited by swans and cranes.
ramayana-6-46-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. The epic pictures the battlefield as a grim river; the app keeps the image brief.

ramayana-6-46-29.translation: Demons and monkey chiefs crossed that hard river as elephant leaders cross a lotus pond dusted with pollen.
ramayana-6-46-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. The epic pictures the battlefield as a grim river; the app keeps the image brief.

ramayana-6-46-30.translation: Then Nila saw Prahasta standing in his chariot, shooting floods of arrows and striking down monkeys.
ramayana-6-46-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-31.translation: As the unassailable Prahasta came on, the mighty great monkey tore up a tree and struck him.
ramayana-6-46-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-32.translation: Struck by it, the bull among demons, angry and roaring, rained showers of arrows on the monkey commander.
ramayana-6-46-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-33.translation: Unable to stop them, he took them with closed eyes, as a bull takes a sudden autumn shower.
ramayana-6-46-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-34.translation: In the same way Nila, eyes closed, bore Prahasta's very dreadful, unbearable shower of arrows.
ramayana-6-46-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-35.translation: Angered by the arrows, great Nila struck Prahasta's thought-swift horses with a great sal tree.

ramayana-6-46-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-37.translation: Those two army chiefs, angry and swift, stood, their limbs wounded, like two elephants in rut.

ramayana-6-46-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-39.translation: Victorious heroes who never turned back in battle, wanting fame, they were like Vritra and Indra.
ramayana-6-46-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-40.translation: Then Prahasta, with great effort, struck Nila on the forehead with his club, and Nila was wounded.
ramayana-6-46-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-41.translation: Then, wounded, the great monkey angrily seized a huge tree and hurled it at Prahasta's chest.
ramayana-6-46-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-42.translation: Ignoring the blow, the strong one took his great club and rushed at the strong monkey Nila.
ramayana-6-46-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-43.translation: Seeing him coming, fierce and furious, the swift great monkey seized a huge rock.
ramayana-6-46-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-44.translation: Nila quickly brought the rock down on the head of Prahasta, eager for battle, fighting with his club.
ramayana-6-46-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-45.translation: That huge rock, thrown by the monkey chief, struck Prahasta's head hard.
ramayana-6-46-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-46.translation: Lifeless, his glory, strength and senses gone, he fell suddenly to the ground like a tree cut at the root.
ramayana-6-46-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-47.translation: He lay fallen on the field.
ramayana-6-46-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-46-48.translation: With Prahasta killed by Nila, that great unshakable army of demons, now dispirited, went back to Lanka.
ramayana-6-46-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-49.translation: With their commander killed, they could not stand, like water breaking through a dam.
ramayana-6-46-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-50.translation: With that army chief killed, the demons, without spirit, went to the demon king's house and fell silent in thought.
ramayana-6-46-50.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-46-51.translation: Then mighty, victorious Nila, praised for his deed, met Rama and Lakshmana and was filled with joy.
ramayana-6-46-51.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 46: Prahasta fights fiercely and is killed by Nila.

ramayana-6-47-1.translation: When the commander of the demon army was killed in battle by the bull among monkeys, the demon king's army, with fearsome weapons and the force of the ocean, fled.
ramayana-6-47-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-2.translation: Going to the demon king, they told him the commander had been killed by the son of Fire. Hearing them, the demon king was seized by anger.
ramayana-6-47-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-3.translation: Hearing that Prahasta was killed in battle, struck by grief, his mind full of anger, he spoke to the chief demon warriors as Indra to the chief immortal warriors:
ramayana-6-47-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-4.translation: "The enemy must not be looked down on, by whom my commander, who crushed Indra's armies, was killed with his followers and elephants."
ramayana-6-47-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama. Even Ravana finally admits the enemy must not be underestimated.

ramayana-6-47-5.translation: "So without hesitation, to destroy the enemy and win, I myself will go to that wonderful battlefront."
ramayana-6-47-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-6.translation: "Today I will burn that monkey army, and Rama with Lakshmana, with floods of arrows, as blazing fires burn a forest."
ramayana-6-47-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-7.translation: Having said this, the enemy of the king of the gods mounted his chariot, bright as fire, yoked with rows of the best horses, blazing with splendour.
ramayana-6-47-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-8.translation: With the sound of conches, drums and tabors, arm-slapping, shouts and lion roars, and praised with holy hymns, the chief of demon kings set out.
ramayana-6-47-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-9.translation: Surrounded by chief demons like mountains and clouds, flesh-eaters with fiery eyes, he shone like Rudra, lord of gods, surrounded by spirits.
ramayana-6-47-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-10.translation: Coming suddenly out of the city, the mighty one saw the fierce monkey army, roaring like the ocean and clouds, ready with trees and rocks in hand.
ramayana-6-47-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-11.translation: Seeing that very fierce demon army, glorious Rama, with arms like serpent kings, followed by his army, said to Vibhishana, best of warriors:
ramayana-6-47-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-12.translation: "Whose is this unshakable, fearless army, full of many flags, banners and weapons, lances, swords, tridents and discs, with elephants like mountains?"
ramayana-6-47-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-13.translation: Hearing Rama's words, Vibhishana, equal to Indra in valour, told Rama about the best of the great demon chiefs' forces.
ramayana-6-47-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-14.translation: "The great one on the elephant's back, his face copper like the rising sun, shaking the elephant's head as he comes: know him, king, as Akampana."
ramayana-6-47-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama. This seems to be a different hero of the same name, or a variant in the text.

ramayana-6-47-15.translation: "He in the chariot with the lion banner, shaking a bow bright as Indra's rainbow, shining like an elephant with fierce tusks, is the chief of boon-holders named Indrajit."
ramayana-6-47-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-16.translation: "This archer in the chariot like the Vindhya, Asta and Mahendra mountains, a great chariot warrior of great valour, stretching his matchless bow, is Atikaya, huge in body."
ramayana-6-47-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-17.translation: "This great one with eyes copper like the new sun, roaring on a fierce elephant with ringing bells, is the hero named Mahodara."
ramayana-6-47-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-18.translation: "This one on a horse with gold-adorned harness, bright as a twilight cloud-mountain, raising a shining lance, swift as lightning, is Pishacha."
ramayana-6-47-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-19.translation: "This one coming on a great bull like a mountain, holding a sharp trident bright as lightning and swift as the thunderbolt, is famous Trishiras."
ramayana-6-47-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-20.translation: "And this one like a cloud, Kumbha, broad and well-formed of chest, focused, with the serpent-king banner, shines stretching and shaking his bow."
ramayana-6-47-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-21.translation: "This one coming with a blazing, smoking bar set with gold and diamonds, the banner of the demon army, is Nikumbha of wonderful, fearsome deeds."
ramayana-6-47-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-22.translation: "This one shining tall in a chariot full of bows, swords and arrows, bannered, bright as fire, is Narantaka, who fights with mountain peaks."
ramayana-6-47-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-23.translation: "This one, surrounded by spirits of many fearsome forms with faces of tigers, camels, elephants and lions and rolling eyes, is the one who breaks even the gods' pride."
ramayana-6-47-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-24.translation: "Where that excellent white umbrella with fine ribs shines like the moon, there the great lord of demons shines like Rudra among spirits."
ramayana-6-47-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-25.translation: "This one with a crown and swinging earrings, his body fearsome like the Himalaya and the Vindhya, who crushed the pride of Indra and Yama, the lord of demons shines like the sun."
ramayana-6-47-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-26.translation: Then Rama replied to Vibhishana, tamer of foes: "Ah, blazing and mighty is Ravana, lord of demons."
ramayana-6-47-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-27.translation: "Ravana shines with rays like the sun, hard to look at. I clearly see his form wrapped in splendour."
ramayana-6-47-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-28.translation: "The body of the heroes among gods and danavas would not be like this, as this body of the demon king shines."
ramayana-6-47-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama. Rama honestly acknowledges his enemy's greatness.

ramayana-6-47-29.translation: "All his warriors are like mountains, all fight with mountains, all hold blazing weapons, mighty ones."
ramayana-6-47-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-30.translation: "The demon king shines among those blazing, fearsome, sharp spirits like Death with bodily forms around him."
ramayana-6-47-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-31.translation: Saying this, mighty Rama took up his bow and, followed by Lakshmana, stood with the best arrow raised.
ramayana-6-47-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-32.translation: Then the great lord of demons said to those mighty demons: "Stand at the gates, the posts and the gate towers, at ease and without worry."
ramayana-6-47-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-33.translation: Dismissing them suddenly, when the demons had gone to their posts, he tore through the ocean-flood of monkeys like a great fish through a full sea.
ramayana-6-47-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-34.translation: Seeing the demon king suddenly coming in battle with his blazing bow and arrows, the monkey king tore up a great mountain top and ran at him.
ramayana-6-47-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-35.translation: He took that mountain peak with many trees on its slopes and threw it at the night-rover; seeing it come, Ravana split it with gold-feathered arrows.
ramayana-6-47-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana himself goes to battle; Vibhishana names his generals for Rama.

ramayana-6-47-36.translation: When that peak with its tall trees fell scattered on the ground, the lord of the demon world took up an arrow like a great serpent, like Death.
ramayana-6-47-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-37.translation: Taking that arrow, swift as wind, bright as fire with sparks, swift as Indra's thunderbolt, he angrily shot it to kill Sugriva.
ramayana-6-47-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-38.translation: Released from Ravana's arm, the sharp arrow, like Indra's thunderbolt, struck Sugriva hard, as Skanda's spear pierced Mount Krauncha.
ramayana-6-47-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-39.translation: Pained by the arrow, his senses reeling, the hero fell groaning to the ground; seeing him fallen and unconscious, the demons roared with joy.
ramayana-6-47-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-40.translation: Then Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sudamshtra, Rishabha, Jyotimukha and Nala, growing huge, raised rocks and rushed at the demon king.
ramayana-6-47-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-41.translation: The demon lord made their blows useless with sharp arrows, and pierced those monkey chiefs with nets of gold-feathered arrows.
ramayana-6-47-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-42.translation: Pierced by the arrows of the gods' enemy, those fearsome monkey chiefs fell to the ground; then he covered that fierce monkey army with nets of arrows.
ramayana-6-47-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-43.translation: Struck, their best heroes fallen, crying out, pierced by fear, the monkeys, pained by Ravana's arrows, went to Rama, the refuge, for refuge.
ramayana-6-47-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. In trouble, everyone turns to the one who gives refuge.

ramayana-6-47-44.translation: Then great Rama, the archer, took up his bow and went at once; Lakshmana came to him with joined palms and spoke meaningful words.
ramayana-6-47-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-45.translation: "Noble one, you are surely enough to kill this wicked one; but I will crush this base one. Give me leave, lord."
ramayana-6-47-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-46.translation: Rama, mighty and true in valour, said to him: "Go, Lakshmana, and be very careful in battle."
ramayana-6-47-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-47.translation: "Ravana has great strength and wonderful valour in battle; angry, he is surely hard to withstand even by the three worlds."
ramayana-6-47-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-48.translation: "Look for his weak points and guard your own. Protect yourself carefully and attentively, with your eyes and your bow."
ramayana-6-47-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Wise advice for any contest: know the other's weak points and guard your own.

ramayana-6-47-49.translation: Hearing Raghava's words, Saumitri embraced and honoured Rama, saluted him, and went to battle.
ramayana-6-47-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-50.translation: With arms like an elephant's trunk, he saw Ravana with his blazing, raised, fearsome bow, covering the monkeys with nets of arrow showers.
ramayana-6-47-50.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-51.translation: Seeing him, mighty Hanuman, son of the Wind, warding off the nets of arrows, ran at Ravana.
ramayana-6-47-51.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-52.translation: Reaching his chariot, raising his right arm, wise Hanuman, frightening Ravana, said:
ramayana-6-47-52.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-53.translation: "Gods, danavas, gandharvas, yakshas and demons could not kill you, so you crushed them; but your danger is from monkeys."
ramayana-6-47-53.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Ravana's boon protected him from gods and demons, but not from humans and monkeys.

ramayana-6-47-54.translation: "This five-fingered right arm of mine is raised; it will drive out the life that has lived long in your body."
ramayana-6-47-54.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-55.translation: Hearing Hanuman, Ravana of fearsome valour, eyes red with anger, said:
ramayana-6-47-55.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-56.translation: "Strike quickly, without fear, and gain lasting fame. Then, monkey, once I know your strength, I will destroy you."
ramayana-6-47-56.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-57.translation: Hearing Ravana, the son of the Wind said: "I struck before. Remember Aksha, your son."
ramayana-6-47-57.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-58.translation: Told this, mighty Ravana, lord of demons, struck the son of the Wind on the chest with his palm.
ramayana-6-47-58.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-59.translation: Struck by his palm, he reeled again and again; then, very angry, he struck the enemy of the gods with his palm too.
ramayana-6-47-59.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-60.translation: Struck by the palm of the great monkey, ten-headed Ravana shook like a mountain in an earthquake.
ramayana-6-47-60.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-61.translation: Seeing Ravana struck by a palm in battle, sages, monkeys, siddhas, gods and demons shouted.
ramayana-6-47-61.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-62.translation: Then mighty Ravana, recovering, said: "Well done! By your monkey strength you are a praiseworthy enemy to me."
ramayana-6-47-62.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-63.translation: Told this by Ravana, the son of the Wind said: "Shame on my strength, that you are still alive, Ravana."
ramayana-6-47-63.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-64.translation: "Strike once more now, fool; why boast? Then my fist will send you to Yama's realm." At the Wind's son's words, his anger blazed.
ramayana-6-47-64.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-65.translation: Eyes red, the mighty one raised his right fist with effort and brought it down hard on the monkey's broad chest; struck again, Hanuman reeled.
ramayana-6-47-65.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-66.translation: Seeing mighty Hanuman dazed, the great chariot fighter quickly drove his chariot toward Nila.
ramayana-6-47-66.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-67.translation: With fearsome serpent-like arrows piercing vital points, he burned Nila, commander of the monkey army.
ramayana-6-47-67.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-68.translation: Hurt by the flood of arrows, Nila, commander of the monkeys, threw a mountain peak at the demon lord with one hand.
ramayana-6-47-68.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-69.translation: Mighty Hanuman too, recovering, great-hearted, looking about eager for battle, said angrily:
ramayana-6-47-69.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-70.translation: "It is not right to rush at Ravana, lord of demons, while he is fighting another, Nila."
ramayana-6-47-70.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Hanuman will not attack someone already engaged with another; fair play even in war.

ramayana-6-47-71.translation: Mighty Ravana struck that peak with seven sharp arrows, and it fell scattered.

ramayana-6-47-77.translation: Seeing that monkey on the banner top, the bow tip and the crown tip, Lakshmana, Hanuman and Rama were amazed.

ramayana-6-47-78.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-79.translation: Then the monkeys, seeing their chance, shouted joyfully, seeing Ravana confused by Nila's quickness in battle.

ramayana-6-47-80.translation: Angered by the monkeys' noise, Ravana, his heart full of confusion, did not know what to do.

ramayana-6-47-81.translation: Taking an arrow joined with the fire weapon, the night-rover Ravana looked at Nila on his banner top.
ramayana-6-47-81.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-82.translation: Then mighty Ravana said: "Monkey, you are quick, with this great trickery."
ramayana-6-47-82.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-83.translation: "Save your life if you can, monkey. You create these many forms of yourself again and again."
ramayana-6-47-83.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-84.translation: "Still, the arrow I release, charged with the weapon, will take your life even as you try to guard it."
ramayana-6-47-84.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-85.translation: Saying this, mighty-armed Ravana, lord of demons, fitted the arrow with the weapon and struck the commander.

ramayana-6-47-86.translation: Struck in the chest by the weapon-charged arrow, Nila, burning, fell suddenly to the ground.
ramayana-6-47-86.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-87.translation: Through his father's greatness and his own strength, he fell to his knees on the ground but did not lose his life.
ramayana-6-47-87.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Nila is protected because his father is Fire.

ramayana-6-47-88.translation: Seeing the monkey unconscious, ten-headed Ravana, eager for battle, rushed at Saumitri in his chariot roaring like a cloud.
ramayana-6-47-88.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-89.translation: Saumitri, of undaunted spirit, stretching his matchless bow, said: "Come to me, lord of night-rovers; you should not fight the monkeys."
ramayana-6-47-89.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-90.translation: Hearing his full-voiced words and the fierce sound of his bowstring, the king came up to Saumitri standing there and angrily said:
ramayana-6-47-90.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-91.translation: "Luckily, Raghava, you have come within my sight, heading for death, your mind turned wrong. This moment you will go to the land of death, struck by my nets of arrows."
ramayana-6-47-91.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-92.translation: Unsurprised, Saumitri said to him as he roared with his white-tipped fangs bared: "King, the truly mighty do not roar. You boast, best of evildoers."
ramayana-6-47-92.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. True strength does not need to boast.

ramayana-6-47-93.translation: "I know your valour, king of demons, your strength, power and courage. I stand here with bow and arrows in hand. Come; why this empty boasting?"
ramayana-6-47-93.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-94.translation: Told this, the angry demon lord shot seven well-feathered arrows; Lakshmana cut them with sharp gold-feathered arrows.
ramayana-6-47-94.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-95.translation: Seeing them suddenly cut like serpent kings with their bodies cut, the lord of Lanka grew angry and shot other sharp arrows.
ramayana-6-47-95.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-96.translation: Rama's younger brother rained a fierce shower of arrows from his bow; with razor, crescent, karni and bhalla arrows he cut Ravana's arrows and was not shaken.
ramayana-6-47-96.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-97.translation: Lakshmana quickly fitted sharp, fire-bright arrows swift as Indra's thunderbolt to his bow and shot them to kill the demon lord.
ramayana-6-47-97.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-98.translation: The demon king cut them, and having cut them struck Lakshmana on the forehead with an arrow given by Brahma, bright as the fire of doom.
ramayana-6-47-98.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-99.translation: Pained by Ravana's arrow, Lakshmana reeled, holding his bow loosely; recovering with difficulty, he cut the bow of Indra's enemy.
ramayana-6-47-99.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-100.translation: With the bow cut, the son of Dasharatha struck him with three sharp arrows; pained, the king reeled and with difficulty came to his senses.
ramayana-6-47-100.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-101.translation: Bow cut, struck by arrows, his body wet with sweat, the gods' enemy took a mighty spear given by Brahma.
ramayana-6-47-101.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-102.translation: The lord of the demon realm hurled at Saumitri that blazing spear, like smokeless fire, terror of the monkey armies.
ramayana-6-47-102.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-103.translation: Bharata's younger brother struck it with weapons and fire-like arrows as it came; still that spear entered the broad chest of Dasharatha's son.
ramayana-6-47-103.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-104.translation: Struck in the chest by Brahma's spear, Saumitri remembered himself as an unthinkable part of Vishnu.
ramayana-6-47-104.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Lakshmana is said to be a portion of Vishnu.

ramayana-6-47-105.translation: Then the thorn of the gods pressed Saumitri, crusher of the danavas' pride, with his arms, but could not lift him.
ramayana-6-47-105.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-106.translation: Himalaya, Mandara, Meru, or the three worlds with the gods could be lifted by his arms, but not Bharata's younger brother in battle.
ramayana-6-47-106.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-107.translation: Seeing Lakshmana, a part of Vishnu in human body, unconscious, Ravana was amazed.
ramayana-6-47-107.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-108.translation: Then the son of the Wind, angry, ran at Ravana and struck him on the chest with a fist like a thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-47-108.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-109.translation: With that blow of the fist, Ravana, lord of demons, fell to his knees on the ground, swayed and collapsed.
ramayana-6-47-109.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-110.translation: Seeing Ravana of fearsome valour unconscious in battle, the sages, the monkeys and the gods with Indra shouted.
ramayana-6-47-110.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-111.translation: Mighty Hanuman took Lakshmana, struck by Ravana, in his arms and carried him to Raghava.
ramayana-6-47-111.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-112.translation: Through the Wind's son's friendship and great devotion, he who could not be moved by enemies became light for the monkey.
ramayana-6-47-112.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. What enemies could not move, love could carry easily.

ramayana-6-47-113.translation: Leaving Saumitri, unbeatable in battle, that spear went back to its place in Ravana's chariot.
ramayana-6-47-113.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-114.translation: Mighty Ravana too, regaining his senses in the great battle, took up sharp arrows and a great bow.
ramayana-6-47-114.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-115.translation: Lakshmana, killer of foes, recovered and free of the spear, remembered himself as the unthinkable part of Vishnu.
ramayana-6-47-115.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-116.translation: Seeing the great monkey army with its great heroes struck down, Raghava rushed at Ravana in battle.
ramayana-6-47-116.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-117.translation: Then Hanuman came to him and said: "Climb on my back and punish the demon."
ramayana-6-47-117.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-118.translation: Hearing these words of the Wind's son, the hero at once climbed onto the great monkey Hanuman; the lord of men saw Ravana in his chariot in battle.
ramayana-6-47-118.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. A beloved image: Rama fighting from Hanuman's shoulders.

ramayana-6-47-119.translation: Seeing him, mighty Raghava rushed at him, like angry Vishnu with raised weapon at Virochana's son.
ramayana-6-47-119.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-120.translation: He twanged his bowstring loudly, with a sound like a thunderbolt crashing, and Rama said to the demon king in a deep voice:
ramayana-6-47-120.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-121.translation: "Stop, stop! Having done such a wrong to me, where will you go, tiger among demons, and find release?"
ramayana-6-47-121.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-122.translation: "Even if you go to Indra, Yama, the Sun, Brahma, Agni or Shankara, or to the ten directions, you will not escape me today."
ramayana-6-47-122.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-123.translation: "And he whom you struck with the spear today, who suddenly fell into despair: that same one, king of demons, will be death to you, your sons and wives in battle."
ramayana-6-47-123.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-124.translation: Hearing Raghava's words, the demon king struck the great monkey with sharp arrows like the flames of the fire of doom.
ramayana-6-47-124.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-125.translation: Though struck by the demon's arrows in battle, Hanuman, full of natural energy, grew even more powerful.
ramayana-6-47-125.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-126.translation: Then mighty Rama, seeing the tiger among monkeys wounded by Ravana, came under anger's power.
ramayana-6-47-126.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-127.translation: Attacking Ravana's chariot, Rama cut it with well-feathered arrows, with its wheels, horses, banner, umbrella, great flag, driver, thunderbolt, trident and sword.
ramayana-6-47-127.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-128.translation: Then he swiftly struck Indra's enemy with an arrow like a thunderbolt on his broad, fine chest, as Indra strikes Meru with the thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-47-128.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-129.translation: The king, who had not been shaken or moved by thunderbolts and lightning, struck by Rama's arrow, was badly hurt, reeled, and let go of his bow.
ramayana-6-47-129.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-47-130.translation: Seeing him reeling, great Rama took up a blazing crescent arrow and at once cut off the demon lord's sun-bright crown.
ramayana-6-47-130.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-131.translation: To the demon king, now like a snake without venom, like the sun with its light gone, glory gone, his crown cut, Rama said in battle:
ramayana-6-47-131.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-132.translation: "You have done a great and terrible deed, and you have killed my best heroes. So, deciding that you are tired, I will not send you to death with my arrows."
ramayana-6-47-132.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. Rama will not strike a tired, defenceless foe. Even in war, fairness and mercy matter.

ramayana-6-47-133.translation: Told this, his pride and joy gone, bow cut, horses and driver killed, pained by arrows, his great crown cut, the king quickly went back into Lanka.
ramayana-6-47-133.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-47-134.translation: When the mighty lord of night-rovers, enemy of gods and danavas, had gone in, Rama with Lakshmana drew the arrows from the monkeys at the front of the great battle.
ramayana-6-47-134.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama. After the fight, Rama's first care is for his wounded.

ramayana-6-47-135.translation: When Indra's enemy was broken, gods and demons, hosts of beings, the directions, the oceans, the sages and great serpents, and creatures of land and water rejoiced.
ramayana-6-47-135.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana enters the battle, fells Sugriva, Nila and Lakshmana, and is finally beaten back by Rama.

ramayana-6-48-1.translation: Entering the city of Lanka, pained by fear of Rama's arrows, his pride broken, the king was shaken in every sense.
ramayana-6-48-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-2.translation: The king was overcome by great Raghava, like an elephant by a lion or a snake by Garuda.
ramayana-6-48-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-3.translation: Remembering Raghava's arrows, bright as Brahma's rod and like lightning, the lord of demons trembled.
ramayana-6-48-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-4.translation: Sitting on his golden, divine, supreme throne, looking at the demons, Ravana said:
ramayana-6-48-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-5.translation: "All the great austerity I practised is truly in vain, since I, equal to great Indra, have been beaten by a human."
ramayana-6-48-5.meaning: He feels his power was wasted.
ramayana-6-48-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-6.translation: "Brahma's dreadful words have come upon me: 'Know that your danger is from humans.' So it is."
ramayana-6-48-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-7.translation: "I won freedom from death by gods, danavas, gandharvas, yakshas, demons and serpents; I did not ask it against humans."
ramayana-6-48-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep. Pride made Ravana think humans were too weak to matter.

ramayana-6-48-8.translation: "Knowing this, you must make an effort here. Let the demons stand on the posts and gate tops."
ramayana-6-48-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-9.translation: "And let Kumbhakarna, matchless and deep, crusher of the pride of gods and danavas, overcome by Brahma's curse, be woken."
ramayana-6-48-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep. Kumbhakarna sleeps for months at a time because of a curse.

ramayana-6-48-10.translation: Knowing himself defeated and Prahasta killed, the mighty one gave orders to the fearsome demon army:
ramayana-6-48-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-11.translation: "Take care at the gates and climb the walls. Wake Kumbhakarna, who is overcome by sleep."
ramayana-6-48-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-12.translation: "The demon sleeps for nine, six, seven or eight months. Wake mighty Kumbhakarna quickly."
ramayana-6-48-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-13.translation: "For in battle the mighty-armed one is the peak of all demons; he will quickly kill the monkeys and the two princes."
ramayana-6-48-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-14.translation: "Kumbhakarna, foolish, devoted to common pleasures, always sleeps, while I am beaten by Rama in this dreadful battle."
ramayana-6-48-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-15.translation: "Once Kumbhakarna is woken, I will have no grief. What use is he to me, though strong as Indra..."
ramayana-6-48-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-16.translation: "...if he does not help in such a disaster?" Hearing the demon king's words, the demons...
ramayana-6-48-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-17.translation: ...went in great haste to Kumbhakarna's dwelling. Ordered by Ravana, those flesh-eaters...
ramayana-6-48-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-18.translation: ...quickly went, taking scents, garlands and food. Entering that great-gated cave, a yojana long on every side...
ramayana-6-48-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-19.translation: ...Kumbhakarna's lovely cave, carrying every fragrance, they entered the cave with great effort, pushed back by his breath.
ramayana-6-48-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-20.translation: Entering that lovely cave with its golden floor, they saw the tiger among demons lying there, fearsome to see.
ramayana-6-48-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-21.translation: Together they tried to wake Kumbhakarna, huge and asleep like a scattered mountain, deep in sleep.
ramayana-6-48-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-22.translation: His body's hair stood up; he breathed like a snake, frightening them with great breaths, lying there fearsome to see.
ramayana-6-48-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-23.translation: They saw mighty Kumbhakarna with fearsome nostrils and a mouth wide as the underworld.
ramayana-6-48-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-24.translation: Then they piled before Kumbhakarna a huge heap of food, big as Meru, very satisfying.
ramayana-6-48-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-25.translation: The demons made an amazing heap of all kinds of food for him.
ramayana-6-48-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-26.translation: Then the enemies of the gods set pots of drink and many kinds of wine before Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-6-48-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-27.translation: They smeared the scorcher of foes with costly sandal and covered him with divine garlands and sweet scents.
ramayana-6-48-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-28.translation: They spread fragrant incense, praised him, and thousands of demons roared like clouds.
ramayana-6-48-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-29.translation: They blew conches bright as the moon and all roared wildly together, impatient.
ramayana-6-48-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-30.translation: The night-rovers roared, slapped their arms and threw things, making a huge noise to wake Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-6-48-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 48: shaken by defeat, Ravana has his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep.

ramayana-6-48-31.translation: Hearing the sound of conches, drums and tabors, arm-slaps, shouts and lion roars, birds flying in all directions fell suddenly from the sky.
