ramayana-6-55-7.translation: Seizing sixteen, eight, ten, twenty and thirty in his arms, he ran about attacking them like Garuda attacking snakes.
ramayana-6-55-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-8.translation: Hanuman, standing in the sky, rained mountain peaks and many kinds of trees on Kumbhakarna's head.
ramayana-6-55-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-9.translation: Mighty Kumbhakarna split those peaks with his trident and broke the rain of trees.
ramayana-6-55-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-10.translation: Then, taking his sharp trident, he ran at the fierce monkey army; Hanuman, holding a mountain top, stood in front of him as he came.
ramayana-6-55-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-11.translation: Angrily he struck Kumbhakarna, whose body was huge as a great mountain; overpowered by the blow, Kumbhakarna was shaken and wounded.
ramayana-6-55-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-12.translation: Whirling his trident, bright as lightning, like a mountain with a blazing peak, he struck the son of the Wind in the chest, as Skanda struck Mount Krauncha with his spear.
ramayana-6-55-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-13.translation: His chest pierced by the trident, badly shaken, Hanuman roared fearsomely in the great battle, like a cloud thundering at the end of an age.
ramayana-6-55-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-14.translation: Seeing him hurt, the demon hosts suddenly roared with joy; the monkeys, distressed and afraid, fled from Kumbhakarna in battle.
ramayana-6-55-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-15.translation: Nila threw a mountain top at wise Kumbhakarna; seeing it come, he struck it with his fist.
ramayana-6-55-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-16.translation: Struck by his fist, the mountain top shattered and fell to the ground with sparks and flames.
ramayana-6-55-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-17.translation: Rishabha, Sharabha, Nila, Gavaksha and Gandhamadana, five tigers among monkeys, rushed at Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-6-55-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-18.translation: The mighty ones struck huge Kumbhakarna from all sides with rocks, trees, palms, feet and fists.
ramayana-6-55-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-19.translation: Feeling the blows as mere touches, he was not hurt; he grabbed swift Rishabha in his arms.
ramayana-6-55-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-20.translation: Crushed by Kumbhakarna's arms, the fearsome bull among monkeys, Rishabha, fell, wounded.
ramayana-6-55-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-21.translation: Indra's enemy struck Sharabha with his fist, Nila with his knee and Gavaksha with his palm in battle.
ramayana-6-55-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-22.translation: Pained by the blows, dazed and wounded, they fell to the earth like cut kimshuka trees.
ramayana-6-55-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-23.translation: When those great monkey chiefs had fallen, thousands of monkeys rushed at Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-6-55-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-24.translation: All those mountain-like bulls among monkeys climbed onto him as if onto a mountain, leapt up and bit him.
ramayana-6-55-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-25.translation: Those bulls among monkeys struck huge Kumbhakarna with nails, teeth, fists and knees.
ramayana-6-55-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-26.translation: Covered by thousands of monkeys, the mountain-like tiger among demons looked like a hill covered with its own trees.
ramayana-6-55-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-27.translation: Seizing all the monkeys in his arms, the angry mighty one attacked them like Garuda attacking snakes.
ramayana-6-55-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-28.translation: Monkeys thrust by Kumbhakarna into his cavern-like mouth came out again through his nostrils and ears.
ramayana-6-55-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. A strange, almost comic detail: the monkeys escape out of his nose and ears.

ramayana-6-55-29.translation: Very angry, the mountain-like best of demons rampaged, breaking all the monkeys.
ramayana-6-55-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-30.translation: The demon roamed through the monkey armies, wild like the fire at the end of time.
ramayana-6-55-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-31.translation: With his trident in hand, mighty Kumbhakarna shone like Indra with the thunderbolt or Death with his noose.
ramayana-6-55-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-32.translation: As fire burns dry forests in summer, so Kumbhakarna burned through the monkey armies.
ramayana-6-55-32.meaning: Like fire in a dry forest.
ramayana-6-55-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-33.translation: Then the monkeys, struck, their troops broken and leaderless, shaken with fear, cried out harshly.
ramayana-6-55-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-34.translation: Struck again and again by Kumbhakarna, the monkeys, distressed and weary, went to Raghava for refuge.
ramayana-6-55-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. In trouble, everyone turns to the one who protects.

ramayana-6-55-35.translation: Seeing mighty Kumbhakarna coming, the hero Sugriva, lord of monkeys, leapt up.
ramayana-6-55-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-36.translation: Lifting a mountain top and whirling it, the great monkey rushed swiftly at mighty Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-6-55-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-37.translation: Seeing the monkey coming, Kumbhakarna stood facing the monkey king with his whole body open.
ramayana-6-55-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-38.translation: Seeing Kumbhakarna standing there after his attack on the great monkeys, Sugriva said:
ramayana-6-55-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-39.translation: "You have struck down heroes and done a very hard deed; you have overrun armies and won great fame."
ramayana-6-55-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-40.translation: "Leave that monkey army; what will you do with ordinary ones? Bear one blow of this mountain from me, demon."
ramayana-6-55-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. A leader steps forward to protect his people.

ramayana-6-55-41.translation: Hearing the monkey king's words, full of courage and steadiness, the tiger among demons Kumbhakarna said:
ramayana-6-55-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-42.translation: "You are Brahma's grandson and Rikshrajas's son, endowed with famous courage; that is why you roar, monkey."
ramayana-6-55-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-43.translation: Hearing Kumbhakarna's words, he whirled the mountain and suddenly let it go, striking Kumbhakarna on the chest with that thunderbolt-like rock.
ramayana-6-55-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-44.translation: That mountain peak shattered suddenly on his broad chest; the monkeys were suddenly dismayed and the demons roared with joy.
ramayana-6-55-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-45.translation: Struck by the peak, he grew angry, roared with his mouth open, and whirling his lightning-bright trident, hurled it to kill the lord of monkeys and bears.
ramayana-6-55-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-46.translation: The son of the Wind quickly leapt up, caught with both arms the sharp, gold-garlanded trident thrown by Kumbhakarna, and broke it with force.
ramayana-6-55-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Hanuman saves his king.

ramayana-6-55-47.translation: The bull among monkeys joyfully broke over his knee that great black-iron trident, made of a thousand loads.
ramayana-6-55-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-48.translation: Seeing the trident broken, the great demon lord grew angry; tearing a peak from Malaya near Lanka, he went up and struck Sugriva with it.
ramayana-6-55-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-49.translation: Struck by the peak, the monkey king fell unconscious on the ground; seeing him fallen, the demons roared with joy in battle.
ramayana-6-55-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-50.translation: Coming up to the monkey king of wonderful, fearsome valour, Kumbhakarna seized Sugriva and carried him off, as a fierce wind carries a cloud.
ramayana-6-55-50.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-51.translation: Carrying him, like a great cloud, Kumbhakarna, Meru-like, shone in battle like Meru with a towering, fearsome peak.
ramayana-6-55-51.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-52.translation: Lifting him, the hero went on, praised by the demon lords, hearing the cries of the gods amazed at the capture of the monkey king.
ramayana-6-55-52.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-53.translation: Taking the monkey lord, equal to Indra, Indra's enemy thought: 'With him taken, all is taken, Raghava's army included.'
ramayana-6-55-53.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-54.translation: Seeing the monkey army fleeing here and there, and the monkey Sugriva seized by Kumbhakarna...
ramayana-6-55-54.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-55.translation: ...wise Hanuman, son of the Wind, thought: 'With Sugriva seized like this, what should I do?'
ramayana-6-55-55.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-56.translation: "I will do whatever is right. Becoming like a mountain, I will destroy the demon."
ramayana-6-55-56.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-57.translation: "When mighty Kumbhakarna is killed by me in battle, his body broken by my fist, and the monkey king is freed, let all the monkeys be glad."
ramayana-6-55-57.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-58.translation: "Or the king will free himself, even if seized by the gods with asuras and serpents."
ramayana-6-55-58.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-59.translation: "I think the monkey king does not yet know himself, struck by Kumbhakarna's mountain blow in battle."
ramayana-6-55-59.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-60.translation: "In a moment Sugriva will come to his senses in the great battle and do what is good for himself and the monkeys."
ramayana-6-55-60.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-61.translation: "But if I free great Sugriva, he may be displeased, and there would be lasting loss of his fame."
ramayana-6-55-61.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Hanuman respects his king's honour: sometimes the kindest help is to let someone save themselves.

ramayana-6-55-62.translation: "So I will wait a moment for our king's own valour, and meanwhile steady the broken monkey army."
ramayana-6-55-62.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-63.translation: Thinking this, Hanuman, son of the Wind, steadied the great monkey army again.
ramayana-6-55-63.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-64.translation: Kumbhakarna entered Lanka carrying the struggling great monkey, showered with fine flowers from mansions, roads, houses and gate towers.
ramayana-6-55-64.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-65.translation: Then the great one, coming to his senses with difficulty, held in the mighty one's arms, looking at the city's royal road, thought again and again:
ramayana-6-55-65.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-66.translation: "Seized like this, what can I do now? I will act so that it is pleasing and good for the monkeys."
ramayana-6-55-66.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-67.translation: Then the monkey king suddenly attacked Indra's enemy with his fingertips, nails and teeth, at his ears, nose and sides.
ramayana-6-55-67.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-68.translation: Kumbhakarna, his ears and nose wounded, torn and crushed, overcome with rage, his body wet with blood, whirled Sugriva and pressed him to the ground.
ramayana-6-55-68.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-69.translation: Pressed on the ground by that fearsome strength and struck by the gods' enemies, he swiftly sprang into the sky and rejoined Rama.
ramayana-6-55-69.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Sugriva frees himself, just as Hanuman trusted he would.

ramayana-6-55-70.translation: Without ears and nose, mighty Kumbhakarna, covered in blood, looked like a mountain with springs.
ramayana-6-55-70.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-71.translation: Then the great demon Kumbhakarna rushed out of the city again and attacked the fierce monkey army in battle like the blazing fire at the end of an age.
ramayana-6-55-71.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

keywords.meaning: fire at the end of an age

ramayana-6-55-72.translation: Hungry and wild, entering that fierce monkey army, Kumbhakarna in his frenzy attacked demons, monkeys, goblins and bears alike.
ramayana-6-55-72.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-73.translation: Angry, he seized one, two, three or many monkeys along with demons in one hand and quickly threw them in his mouth.
ramayana-6-55-73.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-74.translation: Bleeding, struck by mountain tops, the mighty one kept attacking the monkeys; and the monkeys under attack went to Rama for refuge.
ramayana-6-55-74.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-75.translation: At that time Sumitra's son Lakshmana, crusher of enemy armies, conqueror of enemy cities, angrily joined the battle.
ramayana-6-55-75.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-76.translation: Mighty Lakshmana sank seven arrows into Kumbhakarna's body, then took up and shot others.
ramayana-6-55-76.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-77.translation: Passing Saumitri by, mighty Kumbhakarna rushed straight at Rama, as if splitting the earth.
ramayana-6-55-77.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-78.translation: Then Rama, son of Dasharatha, using the Raudra weapon, shot sharp arrows into Kumbhakarna's heart.
ramayana-6-55-78.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-79.translation: As he rushed on, pierced by Rama, flames mixed with embers came out of the angry one's mouth.
ramayana-6-55-79.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-80.translation: Peacock-feathered arrows sank into his chest, and his great mace fell from his hand to the earth.
ramayana-6-55-80.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-81.translation: When the mighty one saw himself without a weapon, he made great havoc with his fists and feet.
ramayana-6-55-81.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-82.translation: His body deeply pierced by arrows and wounded, he was like a mountain with springs.
ramayana-6-55-82.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-83.translation: Maddened by fierce anger and his wounds, he ran about attacking monkeys, demons and bears.
ramayana-6-55-83.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-84.translation: At that time righteous Lakshmana, thinking over many ways to kill Kumbhakarna, said to Rama:
ramayana-6-55-84.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-85.translation: "King, he does not know monkeys from demons; maddened, he attacks his own and others alike."
ramayana-6-55-85.meaning: He can't tell friend from foe.
ramayana-6-55-85.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-86.translation: "Let the bull-like monkeys climb on him from all sides, and let the chief leaders stand around him."
ramayana-6-55-86.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-87.translation: "Then perhaps the foolish demon, pressed by the heavy load, will fall to the ground and not kill other monkeys."
ramayana-6-55-87.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-88.translation: Hearing these words of the wise prince, the monkeys gladly climbed onto Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-6-55-88.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-89.translation: Angry Kumbhakarna, climbed on by monkeys, shook them off violently, like a wild elephant shaking off its keepers.
ramayana-6-55-89.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-90.translation: Seeing them shaken off, Rama thought, 'This demon is angry,' sprang up quickly and took his best bow.
ramayana-6-55-90.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-91.translation: Taking his bow like a serpent, with a strong string, fierce and gold-adorned, comforting the monkeys, Rama sprang forward with his fine quiver of arrows tied on.
ramayana-6-55-91.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-92.translation: Surrounded by those monkey troops, very hard to conquer, mighty Rama set out, followed by Lakshmana.
ramayana-6-55-92.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-93.translation: He saw mighty, crowned Kumbhakarna, tamer of foes, his whole body covered in blood.
ramayana-6-55-93.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-94.translation: He was rushing at everyone like an angry elephant of the directions, seeking the monkeys in anger, surrounded by demons.
ramayana-6-55-94.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-95.translation: Like the Vindhya or Mandara, adorned with golden armlets, bleeding from the mouth like a raining cloud...
ramayana-6-55-95.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him.

ramayana-6-55-96.translation: ...covered in blood, crushing the monkey army, like Death at the end of time.
ramayana-6-55-96.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Kumbhakarna's rampage; he carries off Sugriva, who escapes, and Rama comes to face him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

keywords.meaning: Death at the end of time

ramayana-6-55-97.translation: Seeing that best of demons, bright as a blazing fire, the bull among men stretched his bow.
ramayana-6-55-97.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-98.translation: Angered by the twang of his bow, the bull among demons, unable to bear the sound, rushed at Raghava.
ramayana-6-55-98.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-99.translation: Then Rama spoke in battle to Kumbhakarna, coming at him like a wind-blown cloud, with arms like great serpents, like a mountain:
ramayana-6-55-99.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-100.translation: "Come, lord of demons, do not despair; I stand here holding my bow. Know me, enemy of Indra, as Rama; in a moment you will be senseless."
ramayana-6-55-100.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-101.translation: Knowing 'This is Rama,' he laughed with a hideous sound, as if bringing down the hearts of all the forest-dwellers.
ramayana-6-55-101.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-102.translation: Laughing hideously and fearsomely, like thunder, mighty Kumbhakarna said to Raghava:
ramayana-6-55-102.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-103.translation: "Don't take me for Viradha, Kabandha or Khara, nor Vali nor Maricha. I who have come am Kumbhakarna."
ramayana-6-55-103.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-55-104.translation: "See my fearsome great hammer, all of black iron; with it I defeated gods and danavas long ago."
ramayana-6-55-104.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-105.translation: "You should not look down on me because I have lost ears and nose; I feel not even slight pain from their loss."
ramayana-6-55-105.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-106.translation: "Show your strength on my limbs, tiger of the Ikshvakus; then, having seen your valour, I will finish you."
ramayana-6-55-106.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-55-107.translation: Hearing Kumbhakarna, Rama shot well-feathered arrows; struck by them, swift as thunderbolts, the gods' enemy was not shaken or pained.
ramayana-6-55-107.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-108.translation: The arrows that cut through the great sal trees and killed Vali, bull among monkeys, though like thunderbolts, did not hurt Kumbhakarna's body.
ramayana-6-55-108.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-109.translation: Drinking those arrows with his body like streams of rain, great Indra's enemy whirled his fierce hammer and checked the force of Rama's arrows.
ramayana-6-55-109.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-110.translation: Then the demon, terror of the gods' great armies, whirling that fierce hammer, scattered the monkey army.
ramayana-6-55-110.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-111.translation: Then Rama took the fine Vayavya weapon and shot it at the night-rover; with it he cut off the arm with the hammer, and the demon roared wildly.
ramayana-6-55-111.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-112.translation: His arm, like a mountain peak, with the hammer, cut by Raghava's arrow, fell into the monkey king's army and struck it.
ramayana-6-55-112.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-113.translation: The monkeys who survived went to the edge, dejected, and with trembling limbs watched the dreadful clash of the king of men and the demon lord.
ramayana-6-55-113.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-114.translation: Kumbhakarna, his arm cut by the weapon, like a great mountain with its peak cut off, tore up a tree with his other hand and rushed at the king of men in battle.
ramayana-6-55-114.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-115.translation: With an arrow joined to the Aindra weapon, gold-adorned, Rama cut off that raised arm with the sal tree, like a serpent's body.
ramayana-6-55-115.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-116.translation: Kumbhakarna's arm, like a mountain, fell to the ground, rolling about and crushing trees, rocks, monkeys and demons.
ramayana-6-55-116.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-117.translation: Seeing him rushing suddenly, roaring, Rama took two sharp crescent arrows and struck the demon's legs in battle.
ramayana-6-55-117.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-118.translation: Even so, opening his mouth like the undersea fire, he rushed at Rama, roaring, like Rahu at the moon in the sky.
ramayana-6-55-118.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-119.translation: Rama filled his mouth with sharp, gold-feathered arrows; with his mouth full he could not speak, groaned with difficulty, and fainted.
ramayana-6-55-119.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-120.translation: Then Rama took an arrow like a sunbeam, like Brahma's rod and Death, the Aindra arrow, sharp, well-feathered, swift as the wind.
ramayana-6-55-120.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-121.translation: Rama shot at the night-rover that arrow with diamond and gold feathers, blazing like the sun and fire, swift as Indra's thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-55-121.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-122.translation: Driven by Raghava's arm, the arrow lit up the ten directions with its own light; looking like smokeless fire, it went with the force of Indra's thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-55-122.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-123.translation: It struck down the demon lord's head, like a great mountain peak, with bared fangs and swinging earrings, as Indra once struck down Vritra.
ramayana-6-55-123.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-55-124.translation: Struck by Rama's arrow, the demon's mountain-like head fell, breaking the guard houses and gate towers and bringing down the high wall.
ramayana-6-55-124.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-125.translation: The demon's huge body, like the Himalaya, fell into the ocean, crushing crocodiles, schools of great fish and serpents, and sank into the earth.
ramayana-6-55-125.meaning: His body falls into the sea.
ramayana-6-55-125.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-126.translation: When mighty Kumbhakarna, enemy of Brahmins and gods, was killed in battle, the earth and all the mountains shook, and the gods roared for joy.
ramayana-6-55-126.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-127.translation: Then the divine sages, great sages, serpents, gods, beings, Garudas, guhyakas, yakshas and gandharvas in the sky rejoiced at Rama's valour.
ramayana-6-55-127.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-128.translation: Many monkeys, with faces like opened lotuses, were overjoyed and honoured Raghava, whose wish was fulfilled, now that the fearsome, unapproachable enemy was killed.
ramayana-6-55-128.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-55-129.translation: Having killed Kumbhakarna, crusher of the gods' armies, never tired in great battles, Bharata's elder brother rejoiced, as the lord of gods rejoiced after killing the great asura Vritra.
ramayana-6-55-129.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 55: Rama faces Kumbhakarna and kills him.

ramayana-6-56-1.translation: Seeing Kumbhakarna killed by great Raghava, the demons told Ravana, the demon king.
ramayana-6-56-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-2.translation: Hearing that mighty Kumbhakarna was killed in battle, Ravana, burning with grief, fainted and fell.
ramayana-6-56-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-3.translation: Hearing their uncle was killed, Devantaka, Narantaka, Trishiras and Atikaya wept, pained by grief.
ramayana-6-56-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-4.translation: Hearing their brother was killed by Rama of tireless deeds, Mahodara and Mahaparshva were overcome by grief.
ramayana-6-56-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-5.translation: Then, coming to his senses with difficulty, the bull among demons Ravana, crushed by Kumbhakarna's death, lamented.
ramayana-6-56-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-6.translation: "Alas, hero, crusher of enemies' pride, mighty Kumbhakarna! Having burned the enemy army alone, where are you going, leaving me?"
ramayana-6-56-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-7.translation: "Now I truly am nothing, since my right arm has fallen, relying on which I did not fear gods or asuras."
ramayana-6-56-7.meaning: He has lost his right arm.
ramayana-6-56-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-8.translation: "How could such a hero, crusher of the pride of gods and danavas, like the fire of doom, be killed in battle by Raghava today?"
ramayana-6-56-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-9.translation: "You, whom even the crash of the thunderbolt could not harm, how do you lie asleep on the earth, pained by Rama's arrows?"
ramayana-6-56-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-10.translation: "These hosts of gods with the sages, standing in the sky, seeing you killed in battle, shout for joy."
ramayana-6-56-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-11.translation: "Surely today the joyful monkeys, seeing their chance, will climb the forts and gates of Lanka everywhere."
ramayana-6-56-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-12.translation: "I have no use for the kingdom; what will I do with Sita? Without Kumbhakarna I have no joy in life."
ramayana-6-56-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-13.translation: "If I do not kill Raghava, my brother's killer, in battle, death is better for me than this useless life."
ramayana-6-56-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-14.translation: "Today I will go to the place where my younger brother is; I cannot live a moment after losing my brothers."
ramayana-6-56-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-15.translation: "The gods will laugh at me, seeing me who once harmed them. How will I conquer Indra now that you are killed, Kumbhakarna?"
ramayana-6-56-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-16.translation: "Now Vibhishana's good words have come true for me, which I did not take in ignorance from that great one."
ramayana-6-56-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right. Too late, Ravana sees that good advice was offered and he refused it.

ramayana-6-56-17.translation: "Since this destruction of Kumbhakarna and Prahasta came about just as Vibhishana said, this dreadful thing shames me."
ramayana-6-56-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-56-18.translation: "This painful result has come from my deed of driving out righteous, glorious Vibhishana."
ramayana-6-56-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right. Our actions come back to us.

ramayana-6-56-19.translation: So, his heart deeply troubled, lamenting pitifully and at length for Kumbhakarna, ten-faced Ravana fell down in great pain, knowing his younger brother, enemy of Indra, was dead.
ramayana-6-56-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 56: Ravana mourns Kumbhakarna and admits Vibhishana was right.

ramayana-6-57-1.translation: As wicked Ravana lamented like this, burning with grief, Trishiras said:
ramayana-6-57-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-2.translation: "Yes, our mighty uncle is killed, father; but good men do not lament as you do, king."
ramayana-6-57-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-3.translation: "Surely you are enough for the three worlds, lord. Why do you give yourself up to grief like an ordinary person?"
ramayana-6-57-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-4.translation: "You have Brahma's spear, armour, arrows and bow, and a chariot with a thousand donkeys, roaring like a cloud."
ramayana-6-57-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-5.translation: "You have often struck down gods and danavas, even without weapons. Equipped with all weapons, you can punish Raghava."
ramayana-6-57-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-6.translation: "Or stay, great king; I will go out to battle and root out your enemies here, as Garuda does snakes."
ramayana-6-57-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-57-7.translation: "As Shambara was laid low by Indra and Naraka by Vishnu, so today Rama will lie, struck down by me in battle."
ramayana-6-57-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-57-8.translation: Hearing Trishiras, Ravana, lord of demons, driven by fate, felt as if born again.
ramayana-6-57-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-9.translation: Hearing Trishiras, Devantaka, Narantaka and mighty Atikaya were thrilled for battle.
ramayana-6-57-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-10.translation: Then Ravana's heroic sons, bulls among demons, equal to Indra in valour, roared, "I! I!"
ramayana-6-57-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-11.translation: All could travel in the sky, all were skilled in magic, all crushers of the gods' pride, all fierce in battle.
ramayana-6-57-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-12.translation: All had strength in weapons, all had wide fame; none of them was ever heard to be defeated in battle.
ramayana-6-57-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 57: Ravana's sons and brothers march out to battle.

ramayana-6-57-13.translation: All were heroes who knew weapons, all skilled in war, all with the best knowledge, all with boons.

ramayana-6-60-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-10.translation: Many mighty warriors with fine bows followed the great one, rejoicing.
ramayana-6-60-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-11.translation: Some rode elephants, some fine horses, carrying darts, hammers, swords, axes and maces.
ramayana-6-60-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-12.translation: With the fearful blare of conches and loud drums, Indra's foe went on, praised by the night-rovers.
ramayana-6-60-12.meaning: He goes out in grand style.
ramayana-6-60-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-13.translation: Under a parasol white as a conch or the moon, the destroyer of foes shone like the sky with the full moon.
ramayana-6-60-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-14.translation: The hero, foremost of all archers, was fanned with fine golden whisks.
ramayana-6-60-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-15.translation: With Indrajit, bright as the sun and matchless in power, Lanka shone like the sky with the blazing sun.
ramayana-6-60-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-16.translation: Seeing his son set out with a great army, glorious Ravana, lord of the rakshasas, said to him:
ramayana-6-60-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-17.translation: 'You have no rival, son. You defeated Indra in battle. How much more will you kill Rama, a mere man?'
ramayana-6-60-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-60-18.translation: Told this by the rakshasa king and receiving his blessings, the hero went quickly by horse chariot to Nikumbhila.
ramayana-6-60-18.meaning: Indrajit goes to his sacred grove.
ramayana-6-60-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-19.translation: Reaching the battleground, the mighty foe-tamer placed rakshasas all around his chariot.
ramayana-6-60-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-20.translation: Then the best of rakshasas, bright as fire, made offerings into the fire with mantras, according to rule.
ramayana-6-60-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-21.translation: The mighty rakshasa chief offered into the fire with oblations, garlands and perfumes.
ramayana-6-60-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-22.translation: There were weapons, reeds for arrows, fuel sticks of vibhitaka wood, red garments and an iron ladle.
ramayana-6-60-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-23.translation: He spread the fire with arrow reeds and lances and took a black goat for the offering.
ramayana-6-60-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. A dark rite for power; the epic shows it as the opposite of Rama's way.

ramayana-6-60-24.translation: At once the fire blazed up, smokeless and bright, showing signs that foretold victory.
ramayana-6-60-24.meaning: The fire gives him favourable signs.
ramayana-6-60-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. An omen in the story; it will not decide the end.

ramayana-6-60-25.translation: The fire rose up itself, flames turning to the right, bright as molten gold, and accepted the offering.
ramayana-6-60-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-26.translation: The best of weapon-masters summoned the Brahma weapon and charged his bow and chariot with mantras.
ramayana-6-60-26.meaning: He calls on the Brahma weapon.
ramayana-6-60-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-27.translation: As the weapon was invoked and the fire fed, the sky with sun, planets, moon and stars trembled.
ramayana-6-60-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-28.translation: Having offered to the fire, bright as fire and mighty as Indra, he made himself invisible in the sky, with bow, arrows, sword, chariot, horses and driver.
ramayana-6-60-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. His power is concealment; Rama fights openly.

ramayana-6-60-29.translation: Leaving his army, he went swiftly among the monkey troops and, unseen, rained arrows like a dark cloud pouring rain.
ramayana-6-60-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-30.translation: Struck by Indrajit's arrows and his magic, the monkeys cried out and fell like mountains struck by Indra's thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-60-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-31.translation: They saw only the sharp arrows; they could not see Indra's foe, hidden by magic.
ramayana-6-60-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-32.translation: The rakshasa covered all directions with sun-bright arrows and brought despair to the monkey chiefs.
ramayana-6-60-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-33.translation: He hurled spears, swords and axes blazing like fire with sparks onto the monkey army.
ramayana-6-60-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-34.translation: Struck by Indrajit's fiery arrows, the monkey leaders looked like flowering kimshuka trees.
ramayana-6-60-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-35.translation: Crowding together and crying out, the monkey heroes, pierced by his weapons, fell.
ramayana-6-60-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-36.translation: Some, looking up at the sky, were struck in the eyes; they huddled together and fell to the ground.
ramayana-6-60-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-37.translation: Hanuman, Sugriva, Angada, Gandhamadana, Jambavan, Sushena and Vegadarshin...
ramayana-6-60-37.meaning: The list of heroes struck begins.
ramayana-6-60-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-38.translation: ...Mainda, Dvivida, Nila, Gavaksha, Gaja, Gomukha, Kesari, Harilomana and Vidyuddamshtra...
ramayana-6-60-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-39.translation: ...Suryanana, Jyotimukha, Dadhimukha, Pavakaksha, Nala and Kumuda...
ramayana-6-60-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-40.translation: ...all these tigers among monkeys the rakshasa pierced with darts, spears and sharp arrows charged with mantras.
ramayana-6-60-40.meaning: All the leaders are struck down.
ramayana-6-60-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-60-41.translation: Having struck the monkey chiefs with maces and gold-feathered arrows, he showered Rama and Lakshmana with nets of sun-bright arrows.
ramayana-6-60-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-42.translation: Rained on by arrows, Rama, of wondrous splendour, treating them like falling rain, looked about and said to Lakshmana:
ramayana-6-60-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Rama faces the storm with calm.

ramayana-6-60-43.translation: 'Lakshmana, this rakshasa chief, Indra's foe, relying on the Brahma weapon, has felled the army and now torments us with arrows.'
ramayana-6-60-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-44.translation: 'Blessed by Brahma, standing invisible in the sky, his body hidden, how can Indrajit be killed today in battle?'
ramayana-6-60-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-45.translation: 'I think this weapon belongs to Brahma, the unthinkable, its source. So, wise one, bear these arrows with me, calm in mind.'
ramayana-6-60-45.meaning: Rama chooses to honour Brahma's weapon.
ramayana-6-60-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Rama respects the creator's power instead of fighting it.

ramayana-6-60-46.translation: 'This rakshasa chief covers every direction with arrows, and the monkey army, its heroes fallen, has lost its shine.'
ramayana-6-60-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon.

ramayana-6-60-47.translation: 'Seeing us fallen and senseless, out of the fight, he will surely return to Ravana's city, taking the glory of the battle.'
ramayana-6-60-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-60-48.translation: Then the two were struck down there by Indrajit's weapons, and the rakshasa, having brought them low, roared with joy.
ramayana-6-60-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-60-49.translation: Having brought despair to the monkey army and to Rama and Lakshmana, he quickly entered the city guarded by Ravana's arms.
ramayana-6-60-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 60: Indrajit performs a fire rite, becomes invisible and strikes down the army, then Rama and Lakshmana, with the Brahma weapon. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-61-1.translation: With the two brothers fallen at the front, the monkey army was bewildered; Sugriva, Nila, Angada and Jambavan knew not what to do.
ramayana-6-61-1.meaning: The army is lost without them.
ramayana-6-61-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-61-2.translation: Seeing the army in despair, Vibhishana, wisest of the wise, spoke to the monkey heroes, comforting them with matchless words.
ramayana-6-61-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. In crisis, a calm voice steadies everyone.

ramayana-6-61-3.translation: 'Do not fear. This is no time for despair. The noble princes lie helpless because they honour Brahma's word, struck by Indrajit's weapons.'
ramayana-6-61-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-61-4.translation: 'Brahma himself gave him this supreme, unfailing weapon. If the princes fell out of respect for it, why despair?'
ramayana-6-61-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-61-5.translation: Wise Hanuman, also honouring the Brahma weapon, heard Vibhishana and said to him:
ramayana-6-61-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-6.translation: 'In this stricken army, let us comfort every monkey who is still alive.'
ramayana-6-61-6.meaning: Hanuman's first thought is to help others.
ramayana-6-61-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Care for the wounded comes first.

ramayana-6-61-7.translation: Then the two heroes, Hanuman and Vibhishana, torches in hand, walked the battlefield together at night.
ramayana-6-61-7.meaning: They search the field by torchlight.
ramayana-6-61-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-8.translation: They saw the ground covered with wounded monkeys lying everywhere.
ramayana-6-61-8.meaning: The field is full of the fallen.
ramayana-6-61-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-61-9.translation: They saw the earth crowded with fallen monkeys, huge as mountains, and with scattered, gleaming weapons.
ramayana-6-61-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-61-10.translation: Sugriva, Angada, Nila, Sharabha, Gandhamadana, Jambavan, Sushena, Vegadarshana, Ahuka...
ramayana-6-61-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-11.translation: ...Mainda, Nala, Jyotimukha, Dvivida and Panasa: Vibhishana and Hanuman saw them struck down in battle.
ramayana-6-61-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-12.translation: In the last fifth of the day, sixty-seven crores of mighty monkeys had been struck down by Brahma's favoured weapon.
ramayana-6-61-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-61-13.translation: Seeing the army, vast as the ocean, afflicted by arrows, Hanuman and Vibhishana looked for Jambavan.
ramayana-6-61-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. In trouble, seek the counsel of elders.

ramayana-6-61-14.translation: They found him, old by nature, covered with hundreds of arrows, the heroic son of Prajapati, like a fire dying down.
ramayana-6-61-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-15.translation: Seeing him, Vibhishana approached and said, 'Noble one, have the sharp arrows not taken your life?'
ramayana-6-61-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-16.translation: Hearing Vibhishana, Jambavan, best of bears, spoke with difficulty.
ramayana-6-61-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-17.translation: 'Mighty lord, I know you by your voice; pained by sharp arrows, I cannot see you with my eyes.'
ramayana-6-61-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-18.translation: 'Is Hanuman alive, best of monkeys, through whom Anjana and the Wind have a fine son?'
ramayana-6-61-18.meaning: His first question is about Hanuman.
ramayana-6-61-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-19.translation: Hearing Jambavan, Vibhishana said: 'Why do you pass over the noble princes and ask about Hanuman?'
ramayana-6-61-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-20.translation: 'Noble one, you have not shown such love for King Sugriva, Angada or Rama as for the son of the Wind.'
ramayana-6-61-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-21.translation: Hearing him, Jambavan said: 'Listen, tiger among rakshasas, why I ask about Hanuman.'
ramayana-6-61-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-22.translation: 'If that hero lives, the army, though struck down, is not lost. If Hanuman has died, then though we live, we are lost.'
ramayana-6-61-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. One true helper can save everyone.

ramayana-6-61-23.translation: 'If Hanuman, equal to the wind and like fire in power, is alive, there is hope of life.'
ramayana-6-61-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-24.translation: Then Hanuman, son of the Wind, came to the old one, bowed respectfully and clasped Jambavan's feet.
ramayana-6-61-24.meaning: Hanuman greets the elder with reverence.
ramayana-6-61-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Respect for elders, even in crisis.

ramayana-6-61-25.translation: Hearing Hanuman's voice, though still in pain, the best of bears felt as if reborn.
ramayana-6-61-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-26.translation: Then mighty Jambavan said to Hanuman: 'Come, tiger among monkeys; you must save the monkeys.'
ramayana-6-61-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-27.translation: 'No one else has the strength; you are their best friend. This is the time for your valour; I see no one else.'
ramayana-6-61-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-28.translation: 'Cheer the armies of bear and monkey heroes, and heal Rama and Lakshmana, who lie wounded.'
ramayana-6-61-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Rama and Lakshmana are not dead: they yield out of respect for Brahma's weapon, and the healing herbs will revive them.

ramayana-6-61-29.translation: 'Go a long way, high over the ocean, to the Himalaya, best of mountains.'
ramayana-6-61-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-30.translation: 'There you will see the golden Rishabha mountain and the peak of Kailasa, destroyer of foes.'
ramayana-6-61-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-31.translation: 'Between those two peaks you will see the herb mountain, shining with matchless light, full of every herb.'
ramayana-6-61-31.meaning: The herb mountain lies between them.
ramayana-6-61-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-32.translation: 'On its top you will see four shining herbs that light up the ten directions.'
ramayana-6-61-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-33.translation: 'Mritasanjivani, which restores life; Vishalyakarani, which removes arrows; Sauvarnakarani, which restores the body's colour; and Sandhani, which joins wounds.'
ramayana-6-61-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-34.translation: 'Take them all, Hanuman, and come back quickly. Revive the monkeys, son of the Wind.'
ramayana-6-61-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-35.translation: Hearing Jambavan, Hanuman, best of monkeys, swelled with strength like the ocean with its tides.
ramayana-6-61-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Being trusted gives strength.

ramayana-6-61-36.translation: Standing on a mountaintop and pressing it down, heroic Hanuman looked like a second mountain.
ramayana-6-61-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-37.translation: Crushed under Hanuman's feet, the mountain sank down, unable to bear him.
ramayana-6-61-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-38.translation: Its trees fell to the ground and caught fire from his force, and its peaks scattered.
ramayana-6-61-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-39.translation: As the great mountain shook, its trees and rocks broken, the monkeys could not stand.
ramayana-6-61-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-40.translation: Lanka, its gates shaking and houses broken, seemed to dance in terror that night.
ramayana-6-61-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-41.translation: Pressing the mountain, Hanuman, huge as a mountain, shook the earth and the oceans.
ramayana-6-61-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-42.translation: Pressing the rock with his feet and opening his mouth wide, he roared loudly, as if to frighten the rakshasas.
ramayana-6-61-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-43.translation: Hearing that wondrous roar, all the rakshasas in Lanka could not move for fear.
ramayana-6-61-43.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-44.translation: Bowing to Rama, Hanuman of fearsome valour set about a great deed for Rama's sake.
ramayana-6-61-44.meaning: He bows to Rama before starting.
ramayana-6-61-44.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs. Hanuman begins every great act by remembering Rama.

ramayana-6-61-45.translation: Raising his snake-like tail, bending his back and folding his ears, opening his mouth wide, he leapt into the sky with fierce speed.
ramayana-6-61-45.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-46.translation: His speed swept away groves, rocks and ordinary monkeys, which fell into the sea as the force died away.
ramayana-6-61-46.meaning: His wake carries things with him.
ramayana-6-61-46.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-47.translation: Stretching out his arms like serpents, mighty as Garuda, the son of the Wind went toward Meru, king of mountains, as if pulling the directions along.
ramayana-6-61-47.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-48.translation: Looking at the ocean with its rolling waves, all its creatures tossed, he sped on like the discus from Vishnu's hand.
ramayana-6-61-48.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-49.translation: He passed mountains, forests, lakes, rivers, ponds and fine cities full of people, flying with the speed of his father, the Wind.
ramayana-6-61-49.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Vibhishana and Hanuman search the field; Jambavan sends Hanuman to the Himalaya for the healing herbs.

ramayana-6-61-50.translation: Following the path of the sun, untiring, the best of monkeys came and saw the Himalaya, best of mountains.
ramayana-6-61-50.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-51.translation: It had many springs, caves and waterfalls, and lovely peaks like heaps of white clouds.
ramayana-6-61-51.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-52.translation: Reaching that great mountain with its towering peaks, he saw holy hermitages served by gods and sages.
ramayana-6-61-52.meaning: Holy places lie on the mountain.
ramayana-6-61-52.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-53.translation: He saw Brahma's abode, the silver dwelling, Indra's abode, the place where Shiva loosed his arrow, Hayagriva's shrine, the blazing Brahmashiras and Yama's servants.
ramayana-6-61-53.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-54.translation: He saw the abode of the thunderbolt, Kubera's dwelling, the sun-bright place where the sun is bound, Brahma's seat, Shiva's bow and the navel of the earth.
ramayana-6-61-54.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-55.translation: He saw great Kailasa, the Himalayan rock, the golden Rishabha mountain, and the king of herb mountains, lit by all its glowing herbs.
ramayana-6-61-55.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-56.translation: Seeing it blaze like fire, the son of the Wind was amazed; he leapt onto the herb mountain and searched for the herbs.
ramayana-6-61-56.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-57.translation: Having crossed thousands of leagues, the great monkey roamed over the mountain that held the divine herbs.
ramayana-6-61-57.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-58.translation: But all the great herbs on that mountain, knowing someone had come to take them, hid themselves.
ramayana-6-61-58.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-59.translation: Not seeing them, great Hanuman grew angry and roared; with eyes like fire, he spoke to the mountain.
ramayana-6-61-59.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-60.translation: 'Have you decided so firmly to show no pity to Rama? Then see yourself scattered, overcome by the strength of my arms, king of mountains.'

ramayana-6-61-61.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army. When the exact answer cannot be found, Hanuman brings everything that might help.

ramayana-6-61-62.translation: Lifting it, he flew into the sky, startling the worlds and the gods, praised by many sky-dwellers, mighty as Garuda.
ramayana-6-61-62.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-63.translation: Following the sun's path and holding that sun-bright peak, he looked like a second sun beside the sun.
ramayana-6-61-63.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 61: Hanuman flies to the Himalaya, carries back the whole herb mountain, and its scent heals Rama, Lakshmana and the army.

ramayana-6-61-64.translation: With that mountain, the mountain-like son of the Wind shone like Vishnu in the sky holding up his blazing thousand-edged discus.
