ramayana-6-69-16.translation: Loosing floods of arrows, surrounded by his army, he struck down many tiger-like monkeys, showing his valour.
ramayana-6-69-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Hanuman rallies the frightened monkeys and attacks Indrajit's army. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-69-17.translation: With spears, thunderbolts, swords, axes and hammers, the monkeys also struck down his followers in battle.
ramayana-6-69-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Hanuman rallies the frightened monkeys and attacks Indrajit's army. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-69-18.translation: With whole sal trees and rocks, mighty Hanuman brought havoc on the rakshasas of fearsome deeds.
ramayana-6-69-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Hanuman rallies the frightened monkeys and attacks Indrajit's army. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-69-19.translation: Holding back the enemy, Hanuman told the forest-dwellers: 'Turn back. This army is not our goal.'
ramayana-6-69-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite.

ramayana-6-69-20.translation: 'We risked our lives striving to please Rama; but Janaka's daughter, for whom we fight, is slain.'
ramayana-6-69-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-69-21.translation: 'Let us tell this to Rama and Sugriva, and do whatever they decide.'
ramayana-6-69-21.meaning: They must report to their leaders.
ramayana-6-69-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite. In a crisis, report honestly to those who lead.

ramayana-6-69-22.translation: Saying this, the best of monkeys held back all the monkeys and, unafraid, slowly withdrew with his army.
ramayana-6-69-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite.

ramayana-6-69-23.translation: Seeing Hanuman go to where Rama was, Indrajit went to Nikumbhila and made offerings into the fire.
ramayana-6-69-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite.

ramayana-6-69-24.translation: At the sacrificial ground the fire, fed duly by the rakshasa with offerings, blazed up.
ramayana-6-69-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite.

ramayana-6-69-25.translation: Wrapped in flames and fed with offerings, that fierce fire rose like the sun at twilight.
ramayana-6-69-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite.

ramayana-6-69-26.translation: Then Indrajit offered oblations duly for the rakshasas' welfare, and the rakshasas who knew right and wrong policy stood watching in great crowds.
ramayana-6-69-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 69: Believing Sita slain, Hanuman withdraws the army to tell Rama, while Indrajit goes to Nikumbhila for his fire rite.

ramayana-6-70-1.translation: Hearing the great noise of battle between rakshasas and forest-dwellers, Rama spoke to Jambavan.
ramayana-6-70-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-2.translation: 'Gentle one, surely Hanuman has done a very hard deed, for a great and fearful sound of weapons is heard.'
ramayana-6-70-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-3.translation: 'Go quickly with your army, lord of bears, and help that best of monkeys in his fight.'
ramayana-6-70-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Rama always sends help to those who are struggling.

ramayana-6-70-4.translation: Saying 'So be it', the king of bears went with his army to the western gate where Hanuman was.
ramayana-6-70-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-5.translation: On the way, the lord of bears saw Hanuman coming, surrounded by tired, panting monkeys who had fought.
ramayana-6-70-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-6.translation: Seeing on the road that fearsome bear army, dark as clouds, ready to fight, Hanuman stopped it and turned it back.
ramayana-6-70-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-7.translation: Coming quickly to Rama with that monkey army, the famous Hanuman, full of sorrow, said:
ramayana-6-70-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-8.translation: 'While we fought and watched, Indrajit, son of Ravana, killed the weeping Sita.'
ramayana-6-70-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-70-9.translation: 'Seeing her, my mind was shaken and I was in despair, foe-tamer. So I came to tell you what happened.'
ramayana-6-70-9.meaning: He is honest about his shock.
ramayana-6-70-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-70-10.translation: Hearing his words, Rama, overcome by grief, fell to the ground like a tree cut at the root.
ramayana-6-70-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-70-11.translation: Seeing godlike Rama fallen, the best monkeys sprang up and rushed to him from all sides.
ramayana-6-70-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-12.translation: They sprinkled him with water fragrant with lotuses, as he burned like an unbearable fire suddenly risen.
ramayana-6-70-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-13.translation: Then Lakshmana, deeply grieved, embraced Rama with both arms and spoke to him, troubled as he was, words full of reasoning.
ramayana-6-70-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power.

ramayana-6-70-14.translation: 'Noble one, you keep to the good path and have mastered your senses, yet dharma cannot save you from misfortune; it is useless.'
ramayana-6-70-14.meaning: Lakshmana doubts dharma in his grief.
ramayana-6-70-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-15.translation: 'Things that move and things that do not move can be seen; dharma cannot be seen in the same way. So I think it does not exist.'
ramayana-6-70-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-16.translation: 'If it were as real as the seen world, one like you would not suffer.'
ramayana-6-70-16.meaning: He argues good people should not suffer.
ramayana-6-70-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-17.translation: 'If wrongdoing were real, Ravana would go to hell; and you, devoted to dharma, would not meet such misfortune.'
ramayana-6-70-17.meaning: He points to the unfairness he sees.
ramayana-6-70-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-18.translation: 'Since he has no misfortune and you have fallen into it, it seems right does not lead to right, nor wrong to wrong.'
ramayana-6-70-18.meaning: He says results do not match deeds.
ramayana-6-70-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-19.translation: 'If those who love wrong were punished, and those who do right were rewarded, their fruits would match.'
ramayana-6-70-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-20.translation: 'Since those in whom wrong is rooted prosper, and the righteous suffer, both right and wrong seem meaningless.'
ramayana-6-70-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-21.translation: 'If sinners are killed by wrong, then that wrong is itself struck down by its own act; once struck down, whom will it kill?'
ramayana-6-70-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-22.translation: 'Or if one kills or is killed by fate, then fate is stained, not the person by the sinful act.'
ramayana-6-70-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-23.translation: 'How can one reach the highest through dharma, which is unseen, unmanifest, and both real and unreal?'
ramayana-6-70-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-24.translation: 'Best of the good, if goodness were real, no harm would come to you. Since this has happened to you, goodness seems not to hold.'
ramayana-6-70-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-25.translation: 'Or dharma is weak and follows strength. A weak thing without bounds should not be served, I think.'
ramayana-6-70-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-26.translation: 'If dharma is only a quality of strength in action, then set dharma aside and act by strength as you did by dharma.'
ramayana-6-70-26.meaning: He urges Rama to rely on force.
ramayana-6-70-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-27.translation: 'If dharma is speaking truth, why did you not restrain our father, who was untrue and pitiless to you?'
ramayana-6-70-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end. Rama kept his father's word out of love and duty.

ramayana-6-70-28.translation: 'If dharma or wrong were real, Indra would not have killed a sage and then performed a sacrifice.'
ramayana-6-70-28.meaning: He gives an example from legend.
ramayana-6-70-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-29.translation: 'Dharma joined with wrong destroys, Rama; a man does all this as he pleases.'
ramayana-6-70-29.meaning: He says people do as they like.
ramayana-6-70-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-30.translation: 'This is my view, dear Rama: by giving up the kingdom then, you cut the root of dharma.'
ramayana-6-70-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-31.translation: 'From wealth grown and gathered here and there, all actions flow, like rivers from mountains.'
ramayana-6-70-31.meaning: He praises wealth as the source of action.
ramayana-6-70-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-32.translation: 'For a man without wealth and of little power, all actions dry up, like small streams in summer.'
ramayana-6-70-32.meaning: Without means, nothing can be done.
ramayana-6-70-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-33.translation: 'Giving up wealth and seeking comfort, one used to comfort starts to do wrong, and so fault arises.'
ramayana-6-70-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-34.translation: 'He who has wealth has friends and kin; he who has wealth is a man in the world and counted wise.'
ramayana-6-70-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-35.translation: 'He who has wealth is brave, intelligent, fortunate and full of virtues.'
ramayana-6-70-35.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-36.translation: 'These are the faults of giving up wealth that I have told you, hero, since you chose to give up the kingdom.'
ramayana-6-70-36.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-37.translation: 'For one who has wealth, dharma, desire and gain all go well; one without money cannot gain wealth by seeking it.'
ramayana-6-70-37.meaning: Wealth supports all aims, he says.
ramayana-6-70-37.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-38.translation: 'Joy, desire, pride, dharma, anger, calm and self-control all come from wealth, king.'
ramayana-6-70-38.meaning: He claims everything flows from wealth.
ramayana-6-70-38.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-39.translation: 'The wealth by which those who walk in dharma keep this world is not seen in you, like planets on a cloudy day.'
ramayana-6-70-39.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-40.translation: 'When you went into exile, keeping our father's word, a rakshasa carried off your wife, dearer to you than life.'
ramayana-6-70-40.meaning: He traces the sorrow back to the exile.
ramayana-6-70-40.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Lakshmana speaks in shock and grief; the epic does not endorse these doubts, and Rama's steady path of dharma is shown to be right in the end.

ramayana-6-70-41.translation: 'So today I will remove by action this great sorrow caused by Indrajit. Rise, Rama!'
ramayana-6-70-41.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. Whatever his doubts, Lakshmana's love turns into resolve to act.

ramayana-6-70-42.translation: 'Sinless one, for your sake, angry at the sight of Janaka's daughter's death, I will strike down Lanka with its horses, elephants, chariots and rakshasa king.'
ramayana-6-70-42.meaning: He vows to fight for Rama.
ramayana-6-70-42.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 70: Hanuman tells Rama that Sita has been slain; Rama faints, and Lakshmana, in grief and anger, questions whether dharma has any power. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-71-1.translation: As loving Lakshmana comforted Rama, Vibhishana came there after posting the troops in their places.
ramayana-6-71-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-2.translation: He was surrounded by four heroic ministers with many weapons, like an elephant leader among dark elephants.
ramayana-6-71-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-3.translation: Coming to great Rama, sunk in grief, he saw the monkeys with eyes full of tears.
ramayana-6-71-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-4.translation: He saw great Rama, joy of the Ikshvakus, unconscious, resting in Lakshmana's lap.
ramayana-6-71-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-5.translation: Seeing Rama ashamed and burning with grief, Vibhishana, pained within, asked, 'What is this?'
ramayana-6-71-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-6.translation: Looking at Vibhishana, Sugriva and the monkeys, Lakshmana, in tears, said:
ramayana-6-71-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-7.translation: 'Gentle one, hearing from Hanuman that Indrajit has killed Sita here, Rama fainted.'
ramayana-6-71-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-71-8.translation: Stopping Lakshmana as he spoke, Vibhishana said these meaningful words to Rama, who lay senseless.
ramayana-6-71-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-9.translation: 'King of men, what Hanuman told you in distress I think is as impossible as the ocean drying up.'
ramayana-6-71-9.meaning: Vibhishana says it cannot be true.
ramayana-6-71-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-71-10.translation: 'I know wicked Ravana's mind about Sita, mighty-armed one. He will not let her be killed.'
ramayana-6-71-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-71-11.translation: 'Though I begged him many times for his own good to release Vaidehi, he did not do it.'
ramayana-6-71-11.meaning: Ravana will not let her go.
ramayana-6-71-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-12.translation: 'Not by persuasion, division, gifts or war can anyone even see her, let alone harm her.'
ramayana-6-71-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-71-13.translation: 'Having fooled the monkeys, that rakshasa has gone back to the shrine called Nikumbhila to perform his fire rite.'
ramayana-6-71-13.meaning: It was a trick to buy time.
ramayana-6-71-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-71-14.translation: 'Once he has made his offering, Ravana's son becomes hard to defeat in battle even for the gods and Indra.'
ramayana-6-71-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-15.translation: 'He surely used this illusion to deceive us and to block the monkeys' efforts. Let us go there with the army before it is finished.'
ramayana-6-71-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove. A teaching: see through deception and act in time.

ramayana-6-71-16.translation: 'Give up this false grief, tiger among men. The whole army sinks when it sees you worn by sorrow.'
ramayana-6-71-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. A leader's calm keeps the people steady.

ramayana-6-71-17.translation: 'Stay here with a steady heart and firm spirit; send Lakshmana with us and the army.'
ramayana-6-71-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-18.translation: 'This tiger among men will make Ravana's son abandon that rite with sharp arrows; then he can be killed.'
ramayana-6-71-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-19.translation: 'His sharp, feathered arrows, fierce as birds of prey, will strike him.'
ramayana-6-71-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-71-20.translation: 'So, mighty-armed one, command Lakshmana of good signs to destroy the rakshasa, as Indra wields his thunderbolt.'
ramayana-6-71-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-21.translation: 'Best of men, there must be no delay in destroying the enemy. Send forth your arrow for his death as Indra did against the asuras' cities.'
ramayana-6-71-21.meaning: There is no time to lose.
ramayana-6-71-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-71-22.translation: 'Once his rite is complete, that rakshasa becomes invisible in battle to gods and asuras; if he fights then, even the gods will be in great danger.'
ramayana-6-71-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 71: Vibhishana tells Rama the slaying was an illusion and urges an attack on Indrajit's rite at Nikumbhila.

ramayana-6-72-1.translation: Hearing his words, Rama, worn by grief, did not clearly grasp what the rakshasa had said.
ramayana-6-72-1.meaning: Rama is too dazed to follow.
ramayana-6-72-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-2.translation: Then, gathering his courage, Rama, conqueror of enemy cities, spoke to Vibhishana sitting near, in the presence of the monkeys.
ramayana-6-72-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army. Rama masters his grief to act.

ramayana-6-72-3.translation: 'Vibhishana, lord of rakshasas, I want to hear again what you said; tell me what you wish to say.'
ramayana-6-72-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-4.translation: Hearing Rama, Vibhishana, skilled in speech, said again:
ramayana-6-72-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-5.translation: 'Mighty-armed one, the troops have been posted as you ordered, hero, right after your command.'
ramayana-6-72-5.meaning: He reports the troops are in place.
ramayana-6-72-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-6.translation: 'All those forces are spread out on every side, and the leaders placed in proper order.'
ramayana-6-72-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-7.translation: 'Hear what more I have to say, glorious one: when you grieve without cause, our hearts grieve too.'
ramayana-6-72-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-8.translation: 'King, give up this sorrow that came from a falsehood. Drop this worry, which only cheers your enemies.'
ramayana-6-72-8.meaning: The grief helps only the enemy.
ramayana-6-72-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army. This was a magic illusion; the real Sita is safe in the Ashoka grove.

ramayana-6-72-9.translation: 'Make an effort, hero, and take heart, if you are to win back Sita and defeat the night-rovers.'
ramayana-6-72-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-10.translation: 'Joy of the Raghus, hear my good advice: let Lakshmana go with a large army to Nikumbhila and face Ravana's son in battle.'
ramayana-6-72-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-11.translation: 'Let the great archer, victor in battle, strike Ravana's son with arrows from his bow, like the venom of snakes.'
ramayana-6-72-11.meaning: Lakshmana is the one to do it.
ramayana-6-72-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-12.translation: 'By austerity that hero won from Brahma the Brahmashiras weapon and horses that go where he wishes.'
ramayana-6-72-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-13.translation: 'Brahma decreed: "Enemy of Indra, the foe who strikes you before you reach Nikumbhila and finish your fire rite will be your death." So his death has been ordained, king.'
ramayana-6-72-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-14.translation: 'Order that mighty one to kill Indrajit, Rama. When he is slain, know that Ravana and his friends are as good as slain.'
ramayana-6-72-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-15.translation: Hearing Vibhishana, Rama said: 'I know the fierce one's magic, you of true valour.'
ramayana-6-72-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-16.translation: 'He knows the Brahma weapon, is clever, a great sorcerer and very strong; in battle he can make even the gods and Varuna senseless.'
ramayana-6-72-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-17.translation: 'When he moves in the sky in his chariot, glorious one, his path is not known, like the sun's behind clouds.'
ramayana-6-72-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-18.translation: Knowing the wicked enemy's magic power, Rama said to glorious Lakshmana:
ramayana-6-72-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-19.translation: 'Take the whole army of the monkey king, Lakshmana, with the leaders headed by Hanuman...'
ramayana-6-72-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-20.translation: '...and Jambavan, lord of bears, with his army, and kill that son of the rakshasa, skilled in magic.'
ramayana-6-72-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-21.translation: 'This great night-rover, Vibhishana, who knows that place, will follow you with his ministers.'
ramayana-6-72-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-22.translation: Hearing Rama, Lakshmana of fearsome valour, with Vibhishana, took up another fine bow.
ramayana-6-72-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-23.translation: Armed, wearing armour, with sword, arrows and golden bow, Lakshmana touched Rama's feet and said joyfully:
ramayana-6-72-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army. Before a great task, Lakshmana seeks his elder's blessing.

ramayana-6-72-24.translation: 'Today arrows from my bow will pierce Ravana's son and fall upon Lanka like swans on a lotus pond.'
ramayana-6-72-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-25.translation: 'Today my arrows, loosed from my great bowstring, will defeat that fierce one.'
ramayana-6-72-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-26.translation: Having said this before his brother, radiant Lakshmana, eager to defeat Ravana's son, set out quickly.
ramayana-6-72-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-27.translation: Bowing at his elder's feet and walking around him, he went toward the shrine of Nikumbhila guarded by Ravana's son.
ramayana-6-72-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-28.translation: With Vibhishana, the mighty prince Lakshmana, blessed by his brother, went quickly.
ramayana-6-72-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Vibhishana explains Indrajit can be killed only before his rite is finished; Rama sends Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the army.

ramayana-6-72-29.translation: Hanuman, surrounded by many thousands of monkeys, and Vibhishana with his ministers followed Lakshmana.
ramayana-6-72-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Lakshmana sets out for Nikumbhila with Vibhishana, Hanuman and the army.

ramayana-6-72-30.translation: Surrounded by the great monkey army moving swiftly, he saw the bear king's army stationed on the road.
ramayana-6-72-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Lakshmana sets out for Nikumbhila with Vibhishana, Hanuman and the army.

ramayana-6-72-31.translation: Having gone a long way, Lakshmana, joy of his friends, saw from afar the rakshasa army drawn up in battle order.
ramayana-6-72-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Lakshmana sets out for Nikumbhila with Vibhishana, Hanuman and the army.

ramayana-6-72-32.translation: Reaching there, bow in hand, Rama's brother stood ready to defeat the magic power by the method Brahma had laid down.
ramayana-6-72-32.meaning: Lakshmana prepares to break the rite.
ramayana-6-72-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Lakshmana sets out for Nikumbhila with Vibhishana, Hanuman and the army.

ramayana-6-72-33.translation: He entered the enemy army, shining with many bright weapons, thick with banners and great chariots, dreadful and of boundless force, like darkness.
ramayana-6-72-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 72: Lakshmana sets out for Nikumbhila with Vibhishana, Hanuman and the army.

ramayana-6-73-1.translation: At that moment Ravana's younger brother spoke to Lakshmana words harmful to the enemy and useful for the goal.
ramayana-6-73-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-2.translation: 'Lakshmana, try to break this great army. When it is broken, the son of the rakshasa king will become visible.'
ramayana-6-73-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-3.translation: 'Scatter the enemy with arrows like Indra's thunderbolts and charge quickly, before this rite is finished.'
ramayana-6-73-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-4.translation: 'Kill Ravana's son, wicked hero, devoted to magic, unrighteous, cruel in deeds, terror of all the worlds.'
ramayana-6-73-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-5.translation: Hearing Vibhishana, Lakshmana of good signs rained arrows toward the rakshasa king's son.
ramayana-6-73-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-6.translation: Bears and monkeys, fighting with trees and rocks, charged together at the army standing there.
ramayana-6-73-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-7.translation: The rakshasas, eager to destroy the monkey army, met them with sharp arrows, swords, spears and lances raised.
ramayana-6-73-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-8.translation: A tumultuous clash arose between monkeys and rakshasas, filling Lanka on all sides with a great noise.
ramayana-6-73-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-73-9.translation: The sky was covered with weapons of many shapes, sharp arrows, trees and raised mountain peaks.
ramayana-6-73-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-10.translation: The rakshasas, with twisted faces and arms, struck the monkeys with weapons and caused great fear.
ramayana-6-73-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-73-11.translation: Likewise the monkeys, with whole trees and peaks, struck down the rakshasa heroes in battle.
ramayana-6-73-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-73-12.translation: Struck by the huge, mighty bear and monkey chiefs, the rakshasas were filled with great fear.
ramayana-6-73-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-13.translation: Hearing his army was in despair and hard pressed by enemies, the unconquerable one rose before his rite was finished.
ramayana-6-73-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. The plan works: the rite is broken off.

ramayana-6-73-14.translation: Coming out of the darkness of the trees, angry, Ravana's son mounted his chariot, already yoked and ready.
ramayana-6-73-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-15.translation: With fearsome bow and arrows, dark as collyrium, with red mouth and eyes, cruel, he looked like Death himself.
ramayana-6-73-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-16.translation: Seeing him in his chariot, the rakshasa army of fearsome speed turned back, eager to fight Lakshmana.
ramayana-6-73-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-17.translation: At that time Hanuman, foe-tamer, huge as a mountain, raised a huge tree that was hard to withstand.
ramayana-6-73-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-18.translation: Burning the rakshasa army like the fire at the end of time, the monkey struck it senseless with many trees.
ramayana-6-73-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-73-19.translation: Seeing the son of the Wind destroying them with force, thousands of rakshasas showered Hanuman with weapons.
ramayana-6-73-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-20.translation: Spear-bearers with spears, swordsmen with swords, javelin-bearers with javelins, axe-bearers with axes...
ramayana-6-73-20.meaning: Every kind of weapon is used.
ramayana-6-73-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-21.translation: ...with clubs, maces, fine lances, hundreds of spiked weapons and iron hammers...
ramayana-6-73-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-22.translation: ...with fearsome axes and darts, with fists like thunderbolts and palms like lightning, the rakshasas...
ramayana-6-73-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-23.translation: ...surrounded the mountain-like Hanuman and struck him from all sides; and he, furious, caused great havoc among them.
ramayana-6-73-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-73-24.translation: Indrajit saw the mountain-like best of monkeys, son of the Wind, slayer of foes, striking down his enemies.
ramayana-6-73-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-25.translation: He told his driver: 'Go where that monkey is. If ignored, he will destroy us rakshasas.'
ramayana-6-73-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-26.translation: Told this, the driver went where Hanuman was, carrying the invincible Indrajit in his chariot.
ramayana-6-73-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-27.translation: Approaching, the invincible rakshasa rained arrows, swords, axes and spears on the monkey's head.
ramayana-6-73-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-73-28.translation: Taking those fearsome weapons on himself, Hanuman, filled with great anger, said:
ramayana-6-73-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-29.translation: 'Fight, if you are a hero, foolish son of Ravana. Having met the Wind's son, you will not go back alive.'
ramayana-6-73-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-73-30.translation: 'Fight me with your arms in single combat, if you dare. Bear my force, fool; then you will be best of the rakshasas.'
ramayana-6-73-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-31.translation: Vibhishana pointed out to Lakshmana Ravana's son, bow raised, about to strike Hanuman.
ramayana-6-73-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-32.translation: 'That son of Ravana who defeated Indra has mounted his chariot and wants to kill Hanuman.'
ramayana-6-73-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-33.translation: 'Lakshmana, strike Ravana's son with your matchless arrows that pierce enemies and end life.'
ramayana-6-73-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-73-34.translation: Told this by Vibhishana, terror of his foes, great Lakshmana saw him, mountain-like, of fearsome strength, hard to face, standing in his chariot.
ramayana-6-73-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 73: Lakshmana attacks the army guarding Indrajit's rite; Indrajit leaves the rite unfinished and turns on Hanuman.

ramayana-6-74-1.translation: Having spoken to Lakshmana, Vibhishana, glad, took him, bow in hand, and went quickly.
ramayana-6-74-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-2.translation: Going a short way and entering a great forest, Vibhishana showed Lakshmana the place of the rite.
ramayana-6-74-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-3.translation: The radiant brother of Ravana pointed out to Lakshmana a banyan tree, dark as a storm cloud, fearsome to see.
ramayana-6-74-3.meaning: The banyan tree is the key place.
ramayana-6-74-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-4.translation: 'Here mighty Ravana's son makes offerings to spirits, and only after that does he go into battle.'
ramayana-6-74-4.meaning: This is where he gains his power.
ramayana-6-74-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-5.translation: 'Then the rakshasa becomes invisible to all beings and kills his enemies in battle and binds them with fine arrows.'
ramayana-6-74-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-6.translation: 'Destroy mighty Ravana's son with sharp arrows, with his chariot, horses and driver, before he reaches the banyan.'
ramayana-6-74-6.meaning: Stop him before he reaches the tree.
ramayana-6-74-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-7.translation: Saying 'So be it', mighty Lakshmana, joy of his friends, stood there stretching his bright bow.
ramayana-6-74-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-8.translation: Mighty Indrajit, son of Ravana, appeared in a fire-coloured chariot, armoured, with sword and banner.
ramayana-6-74-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-9.translation: Mighty Lakshmana said to the unconquered descendant of Pulastya: 'I challenge you to battle. Give me a fair fight.'
ramayana-6-74-9.meaning: Lakshmana asks for a fair fight.
ramayana-6-74-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers. Lakshmana fights openly and asks the same of his foe.

ramayana-6-74-10.translation: Told this, the proud son of Ravana, seeing Vibhishana there, spoke harsh words.
ramayana-6-74-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-11.translation: 'You were born and raised here, the very brother of my father. How can you, my uncle, betray your brother's son, rakshasa?'
ramayana-6-74-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-12.translation: 'You have no regard for kinship, friendship, birth, brotherhood or dharma, wicked one, you who corrupt dharma.'
ramayana-6-74-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-13.translation: 'You are to be pitied, fool, and blamed by good people, for you have left your own people to become a servant of others.'
ramayana-6-74-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-14.translation: 'With your weak mind you do not see the great difference between living with your own people and taking shelter with low strangers.'
ramayana-6-74-14.meaning: He argues for loyalty to family.
ramayana-6-74-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-15.translation: 'Whether strangers have virtues or one's own people have none, one's own people, even without virtue, are better; a stranger is always a stranger.'
ramayana-6-74-15.meaning: Indrajit puts family above right and wrong.
ramayana-6-74-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers. This is Indrajit's view; Vibhishana's answer shows that right conduct comes before blind loyalty.

ramayana-6-74-16.translation: 'Only one of our own, brother of Ravana, could be as heartless as you are, night-rover.'
ramayana-6-74-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-17.translation: Told this by his brother's son, Vibhishana replied: 'Why do you boast, rakshasa, as if you did not know my nature?'
ramayana-6-74-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-18.translation: 'Wicked son of the rakshasa king, drop your harshness out of respect for an elder. Though I was born in a family of cruel rakshasas, my nature is not a rakshasa's; good conduct is the first virtue of people.'
ramayana-6-74-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers. A teaching: who you are is shown by your conduct, not your family.

ramayana-6-74-19.translation: 'I take no pleasure in cruelty or wrongdoing. How can a brother be cast out by a brother of a different nature? Yet it happened.'
ramayana-6-74-19.meaning: He was driven out for speaking the truth.
ramayana-6-74-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-20.translation: 'Taking others' property, touching others' wives, and distrusting one's friends: these three faults bring ruin.'
ramayana-6-74-20.meaning: Three faults that destroy a person.
ramayana-6-74-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers. A teaching: do not steal, do not violate another's marriage, do not distrust true friends.

ramayana-6-74-21.translation: 'The terrible killing of great sages, war with all the gods, pride, anger, enmity and hostility...'
ramayana-6-74-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-22.translation: '...these faults of my brother, which destroy his life and power, have covered his virtues as clouds cover mountains.'
ramayana-6-74-22.meaning: Faults hide whatever good one has.
ramayana-6-74-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers. Bad habits can hide every good quality.

ramayana-6-74-23.translation: 'Because of these faults I left my brother, your father. Soon there will be no Lanka, no you, and no father of yours.'
ramayana-6-74-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-24.translation: 'You are too proud, childish and ill-mannered, rakshasa. You are bound by the noose of Death; say whatever you like to me.'
ramayana-6-74-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-25.translation: 'Disaster has come to you today; what can you say? You cannot enter the banyan now, lowest of rakshasas.'
ramayana-6-74-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-26.translation: 'Having harmed the two Kakutsthas, you cannot live. Fight with Lakshmana, god among men, in battle; slain, you will serve the gods in Yama's realm.'
ramayana-6-74-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-74-27.translation: 'Show your raised strength, spend all your weapons and arrows; once in range of Lakshmana's arrows you will not go back alive with your army today.'
ramayana-6-74-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 74: Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the banyan tree of the rite; Indrajit accuses Vibhishana of betrayal, and Vibhishana answers.

ramayana-6-75-1.translation: Hearing Vibhishana, Ravana's son, beside himself with anger, spoke harsh words and leapt forward.
ramayana-6-75-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-2.translation: With weapons and sword raised, standing in his great adorned chariot yoked to black horses, he looked like Death.
ramayana-6-75-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-3.translation: Raising his huge, strong, swift, fearsome bow and touching his enemy-destroying arrows...
ramayana-6-75-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-4.translation: ...he said fiercely to Lakshmana, Vibhishana and the monkey heroes: 'See my valour.'
ramayana-6-75-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-5.translation: 'Today in battle you will try to stop the hard-to-face rain of arrows from my bow, like rain from the sky.'
ramayana-6-75-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-6.translation: 'Today my arrows from my great bow will burn your bodies as fire burns a heap of cotton.'
ramayana-6-75-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-7.translation: 'Today I will send you all to Yama's realm, pierced by sharp arrows, spears, javelins, swords and lances.'
ramayana-6-75-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-8.translation: 'Who will stand before me in battle as I shower arrows with swift hands, roaring like a cloud?'
ramayana-6-75-8.meaning: He thinks no one can face him.
ramayana-6-75-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-9.translation: Hearing the rakshasa's roar, Lakshmana, unafraid but angry, said to Ravana's son:
ramayana-6-75-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-10.translation: 'You have spoken of reaching the far shore of hard tasks, rakshasa. The wise one is he who reaches the end of tasks by action.'
ramayana-6-75-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A teaching: the wise finish tasks by doing, not by talking.

ramayana-6-75-11.translation: 'Without achieving your aim, which no one could achieve, you think by speaking that you have succeeded, fool.'
ramayana-6-75-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-12.translation: 'The way you fought, hidden and invisible, is the way of thieves, not the way of heroes.'
ramayana-6-75-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A teaching: honour means facing others openly.

ramayana-6-75-13.translation: 'Now that I stand within reach of your arrows, rakshasa, show that power today. Why boast in words?'
ramayana-6-75-13.meaning: Show it, do not say it.
ramayana-6-75-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-14.translation: Told this, mighty Indrajit, victor in battles, grasped his fearsome bow and shot sharp arrows.
ramayana-6-75-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-15.translation: Those very swift arrows, like snake venom, reached Lakshmana and fell like hissing serpents.
ramayana-6-75-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-75-16.translation: With very swift arrows, swift Indrajit pierced Lakshmana of good signs in battle.
ramayana-6-75-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-75-17.translation: Pierced deeply by arrows, glorious Lakshmana shone like a smokeless fire.
ramayana-6-75-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-18.translation: Indrajit, seeing what he had done, roared loudly and said:
ramayana-6-75-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-19.translation: 'These sharp feathered arrows from my bow will take your life today, Lakshmana.'
ramayana-6-75-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-20.translation: 'Today let jackals, hawks and vultures descend on you, Lakshmana, when you are slain by me.'
ramayana-6-75-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-21.translation: 'Rama, a lowly warrior, always ignoble and foolish, will today see you, his devoted brother, slain by me.'
ramayana-6-75-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-22.translation: 'Today, Lakshmana, you will lie on the ground slain by me, your armour broken and your bow cast aside.'
ramayana-6-75-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-75-23.translation: To Ravana's son, speaking so harshly in rage, Lakshmana gave a very reasoned reply.
ramayana-6-75-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-24.translation: 'Why do you boast here without doing the deed, rakshasa? Do the deed that will make me believe your boasting.'
ramayana-6-75-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. A teaching: let your actions prove your words.

ramayana-6-75-25.translation: 'Without speaking harshly, without insulting you, without boasting, I will defeat you. Watch, eater of men.'
ramayana-6-75-25.meaning: Lakshmana will let his actions speak.
ramayana-6-75-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. Quiet strength is greater than loud threats.

ramayana-6-75-26.translation: Saying this, Lakshmana drew five iron arrows to his ear and drove them with great speed into the rakshasa's chest.
ramayana-6-75-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-75-27.translation: Struck by those arrows, Ravana's son, enraged, pierced Lakshmana in return with three well-aimed arrows.
ramayana-6-75-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-75-28.translation: A dreadful, tumultuous clash arose between the lion among men and the lion among rakshasas, each seeking the other's death.
ramayana-6-75-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-75-29.translation: Both were strong, both valiant, both bold, both skilled in all weapons.
ramayana-6-75-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-30.translation: Both very hard to conquer, of matchless strength and splendour, the great heroes fought like two planets in the sky.
ramayana-6-75-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-31.translation: Like Bala and Vritra, both invincible in battle, the great ones fought like two lions.
ramayana-6-75-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-32.translation: Standing firm and loosing many floods of arrows, the lion among men and the lion among rakshasas fought with zeal.
ramayana-6-75-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-75-33.translation: Eager to win, bows and arrows in hand, the best of men and of rakshasas rained floods of arrows on each other like two clouds.
ramayana-6-75-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 75: Indrajit and Lakshmana trade words and arrows in a fierce duel.

ramayana-6-76-1.translation: Then Lakshmana, son of Dasharatha, tormentor of foes, fitted an arrow and, angry, loosed it at the rakshasa, hissing like a snake.
ramayana-6-76-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Indrajit and Lakshmana continue their long, fierce duel.

ramayana-6-76-2.translation: Hearing the twang of his bowstring, Ravana's son turned pale and stared at Lakshmana.
ramayana-6-76-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-3.translation: Seeing Ravana's son downcast, Vibhishana spoke to Lakshmana, who was engaged in battle.
ramayana-6-76-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-4.translation: 'I see signs in Ravana's son. Hurry, mighty-armed one; he is broken, no doubt.'
ramayana-6-76-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-5.translation: Then Lakshmana fitted sharp arrows like tongues of flame and loosed them at him like venomous snakes.
ramayana-6-76-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-6.translation: Struck by Lakshmana's arrows that hit like Indra's thunderbolt, Indrajit was stunned for a moment, all his senses shaken.
ramayana-6-76-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-7.translation: Recovering in a moment, his senses back, the hero saw the heroic son of Dasharatha standing there.
ramayana-6-76-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-8.translation: With eyes red with anger, he advanced on Lakshmana and again spoke harsh words.
ramayana-6-76-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-9.translation: 'Do you not remember my valour in the first battle, when you and your brother lay bound and struggling?'
ramayana-6-76-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-76-10.translation: 'In that great battle you both lay first on the ground, senseless, with your leaders, struck by my thunderbolt-like arrows.'
ramayana-6-76-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-76-11.translation: 'I think you have no memory, or clearly you wish to go to Yama's abode, since you dare attack me.'
ramayana-6-76-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-76-12.translation: 'If you did not see my valour in the first fight, I will show you today. Stand firm now.'
ramayana-6-76-12.meaning: He promises to show his power.
ramayana-6-76-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-76-13.translation: Saying this, he pierced Lakshmana with seven arrows and Hanuman with ten sharp ones.
ramayana-6-76-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-14.translation: Then, doubly enraged, the mighty one pierced Vibhishana with a hundred well-aimed arrows.
ramayana-6-76-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-15.translation: Seeing what Indrajit had done, Rama's younger brother laughed it off, saying, 'This is nothing.'
ramayana-6-76-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-16.translation: Gathering fearsome arrows, the best of men, fearless yet angry, loosed them at Ravana's son.
ramayana-6-76-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-17.translation: 'Heroes in battle do not strike like this, night-rover. Your arrows are light and weak; they feel pleasant.'
ramayana-6-76-17.meaning: He mocks the weakness of the blows.
ramayana-6-76-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-18.translation: 'Heroes who want victory do not fight like this.' Saying this, he covered him with showers of arrows.
ramayana-6-76-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-19.translation: His gold-decked armour, shattered by Lakshmana's arrows, fell in pieces in the chariot like stars from the sky.
ramayana-6-76-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-20.translation: His armour torn off by iron arrows and wounded, heroic Indrajit looked like a mountain covered in growth.
ramayana-6-76-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-21.translation: Breathing hard again and again, they fought a fierce battle, both wounded all over by arrows.
ramayana-6-76-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-22.translation: The two best of weapon-masters showed their weapons again and again and filled the sky with arrows of every kind.
ramayana-6-76-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-23.translation: Shooting flawlessly, swiftly, skilfully and well, the man and the rakshasa fought a fierce battle.
ramayana-6-76-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-24.translation: The fearsome slap of their bowstrings on arm-guards was heard separately, like two thundering clouds in the sky.
ramayana-6-76-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-25.translation: Gold-feathered arrows that struck their bodies passed through and sank into the ground.
ramayana-6-76-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-26.translation: Thousands of their arrows clashed in the sky with other sharp weapons, breaking and splitting.
ramayana-6-76-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-27.translation: A dreadful heap of arrows formed in battle, like a heap of kusha grass between two blazing fires at a sacrifice.
ramayana-6-76-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-28.translation: Their wounded bodies shone like leafless shalmali and kimshuka trees in flower in the forest.
ramayana-6-76-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-29.translation: Indrajit and Lakshmana, each seeking to defeat the other, clashed fiercely again and again.
ramayana-6-76-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-30.translation: Lakshmana struck Ravana's son and Ravana's son struck Lakshmana; striking each other, they did not tire.
ramayana-6-76-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-31.translation: With nets of arrows lodged deep in their bodies, the two mighty heroes looked like mountains covered in growth.
ramayana-6-76-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-76-32.translation: Their limbs, red and covered with arrows, shone like blazing fires.
ramayana-6-76-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-33.translation: A long time passed as they fought, yet neither turned from battle nor grew tired.
ramayana-6-76-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires.

ramayana-6-76-34.translation: Then mighty Vibhishana came into the battle and took his place, to ease the strain of the unconquered Lakshmana and do what was dear and good for him.
ramayana-6-76-34.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 76: Lakshmana and Indrajit fight a long, evenly matched duel; neither tires. A true friend steps in to share the load.
