ramayana-6-90-29.translation: The sun, the colour of a sword, very harsh and dim-rayed, appeared with a headless trunk on it, touched by a comet.
ramayana-6-90-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 90: Indra sends his chariot and charioteer Matali to Rama; Rama answers Ravana's serpent arrows with Garuda arrows, while dark omens appear. An omen in the story; the outcome still rests on Rama's courage and right action.

ramayana-6-90-30.translation: Mars stood in the sky over Vishakha, the star of the Koshalas, ruled by Indra and Agni.
ramayana-6-90-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 90: Indra sends his chariot and charioteer Matali to Rama; Rama answers Ravana's serpent arrows with Garuda arrows, while dark omens appear. An omen in the story; the outcome still rests on Rama's courage and right action.

ramayana-6-90-31.translation: Ten-faced, twenty-armed, bow in hand, Ravana looked like Mount Mainaka.
ramayana-6-90-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 90: Indra sends his chariot and charioteer Matali to Rama; Rama answers Ravana's serpent arrows with Garuda arrows, while dark omens appear.

ramayana-6-90-32.translation: Pushed back by ten-headed Ravana, Rama could not set his arrows at the front of battle.
ramayana-6-90-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 90: Indra sends his chariot and charioteer Matali to Rama; Rama answers Ravana's serpent arrows with Garuda arrows, while dark omens appear.

ramayana-6-90-33.translation: Frowning in anger, his eyes a little red, he grew very angry, as if burning with his gaze.
ramayana-6-90-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 90: Indra sends his chariot and charioteer Matali to Rama; Rama answers Ravana's serpent arrows with Garuda arrows, while dark omens appear.

ramayana-6-91-1.translation: Seeing the angry face of wise Rama, all beings trembled and the earth shook.
ramayana-6-91-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-2.translation: The mountain with its lions and tigers shook, its trees quivering, and the ocean, lord of rivers, was stirred.
ramayana-6-91-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-3.translation: Birds with harsh cries circled all around in the sky, calling ominously.
ramayana-6-91-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-4.translation: Seeing Rama very angry and the dreadful omens, all beings trembled and fear entered Ravana.
ramayana-6-91-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-5.translation: Then gods in their sky-chariots, gandharvas, great serpents, sages, danavas, daityas and Garuda's kin in the sky...
ramayana-6-91-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-6.translation: ...watched that battle, like the end of the world, as the two heroes fought with many fearsome weapons.
ramayana-6-91-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-7.translation: Gods and asuras who had come, watching the great battle, spoke with devotion and excitement:
ramayana-6-91-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-8.translation: The asuras cried to Ravana, 'Win!', and the gods cried to Rama again and again, 'Win!'
ramayana-6-91-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-9.translation: Meanwhile wicked Ravana, wanting to strike Rama in anger, touched a great weapon...
ramayana-6-91-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-10.translation: ...hard as diamond, loud, able to destroy all enemies, studded with spikes like mountain peaks, terrifying to see...
ramayana-6-91-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-11.translation: ...sharp-tipped as if smoking, like a mass of end-of-age fire, extremely fierce, unapproachable, hard even for Death to face...
ramayana-6-91-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-12.translation: ...terrifying all beings, rending and piercing: Ravana, blazing with rage, seized that spear.
ramayana-6-91-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-13.translation: The mighty one, very angry, seized that spear by the middle, surrounded by many heroic rakshasas.
ramayana-6-91-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-14.translation: Raising it, the huge one roared terribly in battle, eyes red with rage, cheering his own army.
ramayana-6-91-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-15.translation: That dreadful roar of the rakshasa king shook the earth, the sky and all the directions.
ramayana-6-91-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-16.translation: At the wicked one's great roar, all beings trembled and the ocean was stirred.
ramayana-6-91-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-17.translation: Holding that great spear, mighty Ravana roared loudly and spoke harshly to Rama:
ramayana-6-91-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-18.translation: 'Rama, this diamond-hard spear I raise in anger will at once take your life, you who rely on your brother.'
ramayana-6-91-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-91-19.translation: 'By slaying you, proud fighter, I will today make you equal to the rakshasa heroes slain at the front of the army.'
ramayana-6-91-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin. A boast before battle; the story does not endorse it.

ramayana-6-91-20.translation: 'Stand now; I will slay you with this spear, Rama.' Saying this, the rakshasa king hurled the spear.
ramayana-6-91-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-21.translation: Rama tried to stop it with floods of arrows as it came, as Indra holds back the rising fire of the end of an age with floods of water.
ramayana-6-91-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-22.translation: Ravana's great spear burned up the arrows from Rama's bow as fire burns moths.
ramayana-6-91-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-23.translation: Seeing his arrows turned to ash in the air by the touch of the spear, Rama grew angry.
ramayana-6-91-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-24.translation: Very angry, Rama, joy of the Raghus, took up the javelin made by Indra, which Matali had brought.
ramayana-6-91-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-25.translation: Hurled by the mighty one, that javelin, ringing with bells, lit up the sky like a blazing meteor at the end of an age.
ramayana-6-91-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-26.translation: Thrown, it fell on the rakshasa king's spear; broken by the javelin, the great spear fell, its glow gone.
ramayana-6-91-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Ravana hurls a mighty spear; Rama breaks it with Indra's javelin.

ramayana-6-91-27.translation: Then Rama pierced his swift horses with sharp, very fast, thunderbolt-like arrows.
ramayana-6-91-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Rama breaks Ravana's spear and wounds him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-91-28.translation: With great effort Rama pierced Ravana in the chest with sharp arrows, and in the forehead with three feathered arrows.
ramayana-6-91-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Rama breaks Ravana's spear and wounds him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-91-29.translation: Wounded all over by arrows, the rakshasa king, standing among his troops, looked like a flowering ashoka tree.
ramayana-6-91-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Rama breaks Ravana's spear and wounds him. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-91-30.translation: Deeply wounded by Rama's arrows, the lord of night-rovers grew weary in the midst of his army, yet also very angry.
ramayana-6-91-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 91: Rama breaks Ravana's spear and wounds him.

ramayana-6-92-1.translation: Hurt in battle by Rama's anger, Ravana, proud in battle, grew very angry.
ramayana-6-92-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-2.translation: With blazing eyes, the mighty one drew his bow in rage and, very angry, pressed Rama hard in the great battle.
ramayana-6-92-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-3.translation: With thousands of streams of arrows, Ravana filled Rama as a cloud fills a pond.
ramayana-6-92-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-4.translation: Filled with arrows from his bow in battle, Rama did not tremble, unshakable as a great mountain.
ramayana-6-92-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-5.translation: Standing in battle and blocking his nets of arrows with his own, the mighty one received them like rays of the sun.
ramayana-6-92-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-6.translation: Then the swift-handed night-rover, angry, struck great Rama's chest with thousands of arrows.
ramayana-6-92-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-92-7.translation: Covered in red in battle, Lakshmana's elder brother looked like a great kimshuka tree in flower in the forest.
ramayana-6-92-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-92-8.translation: Stirred by the blows of the arrows, mighty Rama, bright as the sun at the end of an age, took up arrows.
ramayana-6-92-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

keywords.meaning: sun at the end of an age

ramayana-6-92-9.translation: Then, both enraged, Rama and Ravana could not see each other in the darkness of arrows.
ramayana-6-92-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-10.translation: Then heroic Rama, son of Dasharatha, filled with anger, laughed and spoke harsh words to Ravana.
ramayana-6-92-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-11.translation: 'Lowest of rakshasas, since you carried off my helpless wife from Janasthana when I did not know, you are no hero.'
ramayana-6-92-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. A teaching: true courage never preys on the defenceless.

ramayana-6-92-12.translation: 'Having carried off Vaidehi by force while she was alone and sad in the great forest, you think, "I am a hero."'
ramayana-6-92-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-13.translation: 'Hero against defenceless women, violator of another's wife, having done a coward's deed, you think, "I am a hero."'
ramayana-6-92-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-14.translation: 'Breaker of bounds, shameless, unsteady in conduct, having taken on death out of pride, you think, "I am a hero."'
ramayana-6-92-14.meaning: Pride has brought him to this.
ramayana-6-92-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. Pride blinds a person to their own wrongs.

ramayana-6-92-15.translation: 'A great deed, praiseworthy and glorious indeed, was done by you, hero, brother of Kubera, backed by your armies!'
ramayana-6-92-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-16.translation: 'Now receive today the great fruit of that arrogant, condemned and harmful deed.'
ramayana-6-92-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. A teaching: every action brings its result.

ramayana-6-92-17.translation: 'You think yourself a hero, fool, yet you felt no shame dragging Sita away like a thief.'
ramayana-6-92-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-18.translation: 'Had you laid hands on Sita in my presence, you would have joined your brother Khara, slain by my arrows.'
ramayana-6-92-18.meaning: He would not have dared face Rama.
ramayana-6-92-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-19.translation: 'By good fortune, wicked one, you have come into my sight. Today with sharp arrows I will send you to Yama's abode.'
ramayana-6-92-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-20.translation: 'Today your head with its bright earrings will be cut off by my arrows and lie in the dust of battle.'
ramayana-6-92-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-92-21.translation: 'Today the vultures will come down on you as you lie on the ground, Ravana.'
ramayana-6-92-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-92-22.translation: 'Today, pierced by my arrows, you will fall lifeless.'
ramayana-6-92-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-92-23.translation: Speaking thus, heroic Rama, destroyer of foes, covered the rakshasa king nearby with showers of arrows.
ramayana-6-92-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-24.translation: Rama's valour, strength and joy in battle doubled, and so did his power of weapons, eager as he was to end his enemy.
ramayana-6-92-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-25.translation: All the weapons came to the self-knowing one, and in his joy the mighty one became even quicker of hand.
ramayana-6-92-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-26.translation: Recognising these good signs within himself, Rama, slayer of rakshasas, pressed Ravana even harder.
ramayana-6-92-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-27.translation: Struck by the monkeys' showers of stones and Rama's showers of arrows, Ravana's heart reeled.
ramayana-6-92-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-28.translation: When he could not lift a weapon or draw his bow, and his troubled spirit could not answer Rama's valour...
ramayana-6-92-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-29.translation: ...the arrows and weapons he loosed served no purpose in battle, as his time of death drew near.
ramayana-6-92-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-92-30.translation: His charioteer, seeing him in that state, calmly drove his chariot slowly away from the battle.
ramayana-6-92-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 92: Rama rebukes Ravana for stealing Sita like a coward; Ravana weakens and his charioteer drives him from the field.

ramayana-6-93-1.translation: In his delusion, very angry, driven by the force of fate, Ravana, eyes red with anger, said to his charioteer:
ramayana-6-93-1.meaning: Ravana is furious with his driver.
ramayana-6-93-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-2.translation: 'As if I were without strength, unable, without courage, timid, petty, spiritless, without energy...'
ramayana-6-93-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-3.translation: '...as if my magic and weapons had left me, you disregard me, fool, and act on your own judgement.'
ramayana-6-93-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-4.translation: 'Why have you driven this chariot away in front of the enemy, ignoring me and my wishes?'
ramayana-6-93-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-5.translation: 'Today, ignoble one, you have destroyed the fame, valour, energy and trust I earned over a long time.'
ramayana-6-93-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-6.translation: 'Before an enemy famed for valour, whose deeds delight all, you have made me, eager for battle, look like a coward.'
ramayana-6-93-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-7.translation: 'Since in your folly you did not drive this chariot forward, I suspect truly that you have been bribed by the enemy.'
ramayana-6-93-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-8.translation: 'This is not the act of a friend who wishes one well; it is like the act of an enemy. You have not done well.'
ramayana-6-93-8.meaning: He calls it an enemy's act.
ramayana-6-93-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-9.translation: 'Turn the chariot back quickly before my enemy leaves, if you have lived with me and remember my kindness.'
ramayana-6-93-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-10.translation: Spoken to so harshly by the foolish one, the well-meaning charioteer said to Ravana gentle, helpful words.
ramayana-6-93-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-11.translation: 'I am not afraid, nor confused, nor won over by the enemy; I am not careless or without love, nor have I forgotten your kindness.'
ramayana-6-93-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-12.translation: 'Wishing your good and guarding your fame, my mind full of love, I did what seemed unwelcome but was for your good.'
ramayana-6-93-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle. A teaching: a true friend sometimes does what is unwelcome for your good.

ramayana-6-93-13.translation: 'In this matter, great king, you should not blame me, devoted to your good, as if I were some petty, ignoble man.'
ramayana-6-93-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-14.translation: 'Listen; I will tell you why I turned the chariot back in battle, as a river's rush is turned back by the tide.'
ramayana-6-93-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-15.translation: 'I saw your weariness from the great work of battle; I saw no cheer or joy in you, hero.'
ramayana-6-93-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-16.translation: 'These chariot horses are worn out from pulling, sad and exhausted by heat, like cows beaten by rain.'
ramayana-6-93-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-17.translation: 'And in the many omens that appear to us, I see what is unfavourable.'
ramayana-6-93-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-18.translation: 'A charioteer must know the place and time, the signs and gestures, the low spirits, joy and weariness, and the strength and weakness of the warrior.'
ramayana-6-93-18.meaning: A good driver reads his master.
ramayana-6-93-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle. A teaching on good service: notice the needs of those you serve.

ramayana-6-93-19.translation: 'He must know the high and low ground, level and rough, the right time to fight and the enemy's weak points.'
ramayana-6-93-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-20.translation: 'Advancing and retreating, holding and drawing back: a charioteer, who is like family to the warrior, must know all this.'
ramayana-6-93-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-21.translation: 'To give you and these horses rest, and to relieve the terrible weariness, I did what was right.'
ramayana-6-93-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-22.translation: 'I did not drive the chariot away by my own whim, hero; I did it full of love for my master, lord.'
ramayana-6-93-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-23.translation: 'Command me truly what you wish, slayer of foes; I will do it, hero, with a mind free of debt.'
ramayana-6-93-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-24.translation: Pleased by his charioteer's words, Ravana praised him in many ways and, eager for battle, said:
ramayana-6-93-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-25.translation: 'Turn this chariot quickly toward Rama, charioteer. Ravana will not turn back without slaying his enemies in battle.'
ramayana-6-93-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-26.translation: Saying this, pleased Ravana, lord of rakshasas, gave him a fine, splendid hand ornament.
ramayana-6-93-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-93-27.translation: Urged by Ravana's words, the charioteer drove the horses swiftly, and in a moment the rakshasa king's great chariot was before Rama at the front of battle.
ramayana-6-93-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 93: Ravana scolds his charioteer, who explains that he acted out of loyalty and good judgement; Ravana returns to battle.

ramayana-6-94-1.translation: The king of men saw the rakshasa king's chariot, with its great banner, rushing at him with a roar.
ramayana-6-94-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-2.translation: Yoked to black horses, filled with a fierce glow, thick with lightning-like flags, showing weapons like rainbows, it poured streams of arrows like a cloud pouring rain.
ramayana-6-94-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-3.translation: Seeing the enemy's cloud-like chariot coming with a sound like a mountain splitting under a thunderbolt, Rama said to Matali, Indra's charioteer:
ramayana-6-94-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-4.translation: 'Matali, see the enemy's chariot rushing in fury. Coming back with great speed, wheeling to the left, he has made up his mind to die in battle.'
ramayana-6-94-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-5.translation: 'So stay alert and go to meet the enemy's chariot. I wish to destroy it as the wind scatters a rising cloud.'
ramayana-6-94-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-6.translation: 'Drive the chariot swiftly, without fear or confusion, heart and eyes steady, keeping the reins well in hand.'
ramayana-6-94-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. Calm and focus win battles.

ramayana-6-94-7.translation: 'You surely need no advice, used to driving Indra's chariot; eager to fight and focused, I only remind you, I do not teach you.'
ramayana-6-94-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. Rama respects the skill of others.

ramayana-6-94-8.translation: Pleased by Rama's words, Matali, best of the gods' charioteers, drove the chariot.
ramayana-6-94-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-9.translation: Keeping Ravana's great chariot on the left, he covered Ravana with dust thrown up by the wheels.
ramayana-6-94-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-10.translation: Then angry ten-headed Ravana, eyes wide and red, pelted Rama, facing him, with arrows.
ramayana-6-94-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-94-11.translation: Angered by the attack, restraining his anger with steadiness, mighty Rama took up Indra's very swift bow and arrows bright as sunbeams.
ramayana-6-94-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-12.translation: A great battle began between the two, each eager to kill the other, facing each other like two proud lions.
ramayana-6-94-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-13.translation: Then gods, gandharvas, siddhas and great sages gathered to watch the chariot duel, hoping for Ravana's end.
ramayana-6-94-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-14.translation: Then dreadful, hair-raising omens arose, foretelling Ravana's destruction and Rama's victory.
ramayana-6-94-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-15.translation: The sky rained red on Ravana's chariot, and fierce whirlwinds circled to the left.
ramayana-6-94-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-16.translation: A great flock of vultures, circling in the sky, followed wherever his chariot went.
ramayana-6-94-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-17.translation: Lanka was covered by a twilight red as hibiscus flowers, and the earth looked ablaze even by day.
ramayana-6-94-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-18.translation: Great meteors fell with thunder and loud noise, dismaying the rakshasas and harmful to Ravana.
ramayana-6-94-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-19.translation: Wherever Ravana went, the earth shook, and the arms of the rakshasas who fought seemed held back.
ramayana-6-94-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-20.translation: Copper, yellow, pale and white rays of the sun fell on Ravana's body like streaks of mineral on a mountain.
ramayana-6-94-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-21.translation: Jackals, followed by vultures, spitting flame, looking at his angry face, howled ominously.
ramayana-6-94-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-22.translation: A contrary wind blew in battle, scattering dust and blinding the rakshasa king.
ramayana-6-94-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-23.translation: Thunderbolts fell all around his army with dreadful, unbearable sounds, though there was no thunder of clouds.
ramayana-6-94-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-24.translation: All the directions were covered in darkness, and the sky was hard to see through a great rain of dust.
ramayana-6-94-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-25.translation: Mynah birds, quarrelling fiercely, fell by the hundreds toward his chariot with harsh cries.
ramayana-6-94-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-26.translation: His horses shed sparks from their flanks and tears from their eyes, fire and water together.
ramayana-6-94-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-27.translation: Many such terrible, fearful omens arose, foretelling Ravana's destruction.
ramayana-6-94-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama. An omen in the story, foretelling Ravana's defeat.

ramayana-6-94-28.translation: For Rama too there appeared signs everywhere, gentle and auspicious, foretelling victory.
ramayana-6-94-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-94-29.translation: Seeing the signs in himself in battle, Rama, who knew omens well, felt great joy and peace and fought with even greater valour.
ramayana-6-94-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 94: Rama and Ravana face each other; dreadful omens gather around Ravana and good signs around Rama.

ramayana-6-95-1.translation: Then a very fierce, great chariot duel began between Rama and Ravana, terrifying to all the worlds.
ramayana-6-95-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-2.translation: Then the rakshasa army and the great monkey army stood still, weapons in hand.
ramayana-6-95-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-3.translation: Seeing the man and the rakshasa fighting fiercely, all were amazed, their hearts caught.
ramayana-6-95-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-4.translation: Arms busy with weapons, minds amazed, they stood watching the battle and did not strike one another.
ramayana-6-95-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-5.translation: As the rakshasas watched Ravana and the monkeys watched Rama with wide eyes, the armies looked like a painting.
ramayana-6-95-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-6.translation: Seeing the signs, Rama and Ravana, minds made up and anger steady, fought as if without fear.
ramayana-6-95-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-7.translation: 'I must win,' thought Rama; 'I must die,' thought Ravana; resolved, they showed all their strength in battle.
ramayana-6-95-7.meaning: Each knows what is at stake.
ramayana-6-95-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana. Rama fights for victory of right; Ravana senses his end.

ramayana-6-95-8.translation: Then mighty Ravana in anger set arrows and loosed them, aiming at the banner on Rama's chariot.
ramayana-6-95-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-9.translation: Not reaching the banner of Indra's chariot, the arrows touched the flagstaff and fell to the ground.
ramayana-6-95-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-10.translation: Then mighty Rama, angry, drew his bow and set his mind on answering blow for blow.
ramayana-6-95-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Both armies stop to watch the final duel of Rama and Ravana.

ramayana-6-95-11.translation: Aiming at Ravana's banner, he loosed a sharp arrow, unbearable as a great snake, blazing with its own light.
ramayana-6-95-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-12.translation: The arrow struck Ravana's banner and went into the earth; cut down, Ravana's chariot banner fell to the ground.
ramayana-6-95-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-13.translation: Seeing his banner destroyed, mighty Ravana seemed to blaze in battle with the fire born of anger.
ramayana-6-95-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-14.translation: Overcome by fury, pouring out a great rain of arrows, Ravana pierced Rama's divine horses with arrows.
ramayana-6-95-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-95-15.translation: Though pierced, those bay horses did not stumble or stagger; they stayed calm, as if struck with lotus stalks.
ramayana-6-95-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-16.translation: Seeing the horses unshaken, Ravana, angrier still, loosed another rain of arrows.
ramayana-6-95-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-17.translation: Maces, clubs, discs, pestles, mountain peaks, trees, spears and axes...
ramayana-6-95-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-18.translation: ...this rain of weapons made by magic he let fall, and arrows by the thousand, tireless in heart and effort.
ramayana-6-95-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-19.translation: That great storm of many weapons in battle was tumultuous, terrifying, fearsome in sound and hard to withstand.
ramayana-6-95-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-20.translation: Passing over Rama's chariot, Ravana quickly filled the sky and the monkey army on all sides with arrows, loosing them with single-minded heart.
ramayana-6-95-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-21.translation: Seeing Ravana striving so hard in battle, Rama, as if smiling, set sharp arrows to his bow.
ramayana-6-95-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch. Calm confidence in the face of fury.

ramayana-6-95-22.translation: He loosed arrows by the hundreds of thousands; seeing them, Ravana filled the sky with his own arrows.
ramayana-6-95-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-23.translation: With the shining rain of arrows they loosed, the sky looked like a second sky woven with arrows.
ramayana-6-95-23.meaning: The sky is woven with arrows.
ramayana-6-95-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-24.translation: No arrow of Rama or Ravana in that battle missed its mark, none failed to pierce, none was without effect.
ramayana-6-95-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-25.translation: They fought without pause, shooting left and right, and with floods of arrows made the sky seem unable to breathe.
ramayana-6-95-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch.

ramayana-6-95-26.translation: Rama struck Ravana's horses and Ravana struck Rama's, each matching the other blow for blow.
ramayana-6-95-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 95: Rama and Ravana fight their final duel, striking banners and horses, while both armies watch. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-96-1.translation: All beings watched Rama and Ravana fighting so in battle, amazed in their hearts.
ramayana-6-96-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-2.translation: Their two fine chariots, pressing each other in battle, bent on mutual destruction, looked fearsome.
ramayana-6-96-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-3.translation: The two charioteers showed many kinds of driving skill: circles, straight runs, advancing and returning.
ramayana-6-96-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-4.translation: Rama pressing Ravana and Ravana pressing Rama, they moved with speed in advance and retreat.
ramayana-6-96-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-5.translation: Shooting nets of arrows, their fine chariots roamed the battlefield like two clouds pouring rain.
ramayana-6-96-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-6.translation: Having shown many movements in battle, they stood facing each other once more.
ramayana-6-96-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-7.translation: As they stood, the chariot poles met pole to pole, the horses face to face, and the flags touched flags.
ramayana-6-96-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-8.translation: Then with four sharp arrows from his bow, Rama drove back Ravana's four blazing horses.
ramayana-6-96-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-9.translation: Angered at his horses being driven back, the night-rover loosed sharp arrows at Rama.
ramayana-6-96-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-10.translation: Though pierced deeply by mighty Ravana, Rama showed no change and was not troubled.
ramayana-6-96-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-11.translation: The night-rover again hurled arrows sounding like falling thunderbolts, aiming at Indra's charioteer.
ramayana-6-96-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-12.translation: The swift arrows that fell on Matali's body did not cause him the slightest confusion or pain in battle.
ramayana-6-96-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-13.translation: Angered by that attack on Matali, more than if it were on himself, Rama turned his enemy back with a net of arrows.
ramayana-6-96-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them. Rama is angrier when a helper is attacked than when he is.

ramayana-6-96-14.translation: Heroic Rama loosed arrows at the enemy's chariot by twenties, thirties, sixties, hundreds and thousands.
ramayana-6-96-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-15.translation: The seven seas were stirred by the sound of maces, pestles and clubs and the wind of the arrows' feathers.
ramayana-6-96-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-16.translation: With the seas stirred, all the serpents and thousands of danavas living in the underworld were troubled.
ramayana-6-96-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-17.translation: The whole earth with its mountains, woods and forests shook; the sun lost its light and the wind stopped blowing.
ramayana-6-96-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-18.translation: Then gods, gandharvas, siddhas, great sages, kinnaras and great serpents all became anxious.
ramayana-6-96-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-19.translation: 'May all be well with cows and brahmins; may the worlds endure forever; may Rama defeat Ravana, lord of rakshasas, in battle.'
ramayana-6-96-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them. A prayer for the good of all.

ramayana-6-96-20.translation: Then mighty Rama, increaser of the Raghus' glory, set a razor-headed arrow like a venomous snake to his bow and cut off Ravana's head with its bright earrings.
ramayana-6-96-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-96-21.translation: The three worlds saw that head fall to the ground; but another head just like it rose up on Ravana.
ramayana-6-96-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-22.translation: Swift-handed Rama quickly cut off that second head of Ravana with arrows in battle.
ramayana-6-96-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-23.translation: As soon as it was cut, another head was seen again; that too Rama cut with thunderbolt-like arrows.
ramayana-6-96-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-24.translation: In this way a hundred heads of equal brilliance were cut, but no end of Ravana's life was seen.
ramayana-6-96-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-25.translation: Then heroic Rama, master of all weapons, joy of Kausalya, with many arrows in hand, began to think.
ramayana-6-96-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them. When force alone fails, think again.

ramayana-6-96-26.translation: 'The arrows with which Maricha, Khara and Dushana were slain, Viradha in the Krauncha forest, Kabandha in the Dandaka...'
ramayana-6-96-26.meaning: He recalls his arrows' past success.
ramayana-6-96-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-27.translation: '...all these arrows have been trusted in battle. Why then are they weak against Ravana?'
ramayana-6-96-27.meaning: Why do they not work now?
ramayana-6-96-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-28.translation: Thinking this, yet staying alert in battle, Rama rained showers of arrows on Ravana's chest.
ramayana-6-96-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-29.translation: Then angry Ravana, lord of rakshasas, in his chariot, pressed Rama in battle with a rain of maces and pestles.
ramayana-6-96-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-30.translation: As gods, danavas, yakshas, pishachas, serpents and rakshasas watched, that great battle went on all night.
ramayana-6-96-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-96-31.translation: Neither by night nor by day, not for a moment or an instant, did the battle of Rama and Ravana pause.
ramayana-6-96-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 96: The duel rages through day and night; Ravana's heads grow back each time Rama strikes them.

ramayana-6-97-1.translation: Then Matali reminded Rama: 'Hero, why do you follow his moves as if you did not know?'
ramayana-6-97-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-2.translation: 'Loose at him, lord, Brahma's weapon for his destruction. The time of his end foretold by the gods has come.'
ramayana-6-97-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. Good counsel at the right time wins the day.

ramayana-6-97-3.translation: Reminded by Matali's words, Rama took up a blazing arrow, hissing like a snake.
ramayana-6-97-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-4.translation: It was the great, unfailing arrow given by Brahma, which the holy sage Agastya had first given him.
ramayana-6-97-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-5.translation: Made long ago by Brahma of boundless power for Indra, it had been given to the lord of gods when he sought to conquer the three worlds.
ramayana-6-97-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-6.translation: In its feathers was the wind, in its point fire and sun, its body was made of space, and in weight it was like Meru and Mandara.
ramayana-6-97-6.meaning: The arrow holds the powers of nature.
ramayana-6-97-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-7.translation: Blazing in form, well-feathered, decked with gold, it was made from the energy of all beings and shone like the sun.
ramayana-6-97-7.meaning: It holds the energy of all beings.
ramayana-6-97-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-8.translation: Like the fire of doom with smoke, blazing like a venomous snake, it could pierce troops of chariots, elephants and horses swiftly.
ramayana-6-97-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-9.translation: It could pierce gates, bars and even mountains; it was very fearsome, marked by many battles.
ramayana-6-97-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-10.translation: Hard as diamond, loud, dreadful in many battles, terrifying to all, fearsome, hissing like a serpent.
ramayana-6-97-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-11.translation: In battle it was like Yama in form, fearsome, always leaving the field to the birds and beasts.
ramayana-6-97-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-12.translation: It delighted the monkey chiefs and brought down the rakshasas, feathered with many lovely feathers of Garuda.
ramayana-6-97-12.meaning: It brings joy to Rama's side.
ramayana-6-97-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-13.translation: That best of arrows, which ends the fear of the worlds and of the Ikshvakus, takes away the glory of enemies and brings joy to oneself...
ramayana-6-97-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-14.translation: ...mighty Rama charged with mantras and, by the method told in the Vedas, set on his bow.
ramayana-6-97-14.meaning: Rama blesses and fits the arrow.
ramayana-6-97-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-15.translation: Very angry, drawing his bow fully, with great effort he loosed at Ravana that arrow that strikes the vital points.
ramayana-6-97-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-16.translation: Like a thunderbolt hurled by Indra, irresistible as Death, it fell on Ravana's chest.
ramayana-6-97-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-97-17.translation: Loosed with great speed, that body-ending arrow pierced the heart of wicked Ravana.
ramayana-6-97-17.meaning: Ravana is struck through the heart.
ramayana-6-97-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-97-18.translation: Taking Ravana's life, the life-ending arrow passed swiftly through and entered the earth.
ramayana-6-97-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-6-97-19.translation: Having slain Ravana, the arrow, its work done, quietly returned to Rama's quiver.
ramayana-6-97-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-20.translation: The bow with its arrow fell quickly from the hand of the slain one, together with his life.
ramayana-6-97-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-21.translation: Lifeless, the fearsome, radiant lord of rakshasas fell from his chariot to the ground, like Vritra struck by the thunderbolt.
ramayana-6-97-21.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. The long war is over; right has triumphed over pride.

ramayana-6-97-22.translation: Seeing him fallen on the ground, the surviving night-rovers, their lord slain, fled in fear in all directions.
ramayana-6-97-22.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-23.translation: Roaring, the tree-fighting monkeys rushed at them, seeing Ravana slain and Rama's victory.
ramayana-6-97-23.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-24.translation: Pressed by the joyful monkeys, they fled in fear to Lanka, their refuge gone, faces pitiful and streaming with tears.
ramayana-6-97-24.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-97-25.translation: Then the victorious monkeys roared with joy, proclaiming Rama's victory and Ravana's fall.
ramayana-6-97-25.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-26.translation: Then in the sky the gods' drum sounded sweetly, and a pleasant wind carrying divine scents blew there.
ramayana-6-97-26.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-27.translation: A rain of rare, lovely flowers fell from the sky to the earth, covering Rama's chariot.
ramayana-6-97-27.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-28.translation: In the sky was heard the noble voice of the great gods, crying 'Well done!' and praising Rama.
ramayana-6-97-28.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-29.translation: Great joy filled the gods and charanas when fierce Ravana, terror of all worlds, was slain.
ramayana-6-97-29.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-30.translation: Then, pleased, Rama fulfilled the wishes of Sugriva and mighty Angada, having slain the rakshasa chief.
ramayana-6-97-30.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-31.translation: Then the winds grew calm, the directions cleared, the sky became spotless; the earth stopped shaking, the gales ceased and the sun shone steadily.
ramayana-6-97-31.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-32.translation: Then Sugriva, Vibhishana and his dearest friends, with Lakshmana, joyful at the victory, came together and duly honoured Rama, delightful in battle.
ramayana-6-97-32.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice.

ramayana-6-97-33.translation: His enemy slain, true to his vow, surrounded by his people and army, the mighty joy of the Raghu kings shone in battle like Indra among the gods.
ramayana-6-97-33.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 97: On Matali's reminder, Rama uses the Brahma weapon given by Agastya and Ravana falls; the heavens rejoice. Rama kept his word to the end.

ramayana-6-98-1.translation: Hearing that Ravana had been slain by great Rama, the rakshasa women, worn by grief, rushed out of the inner palace.
ramayana-6-98-1.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-2.translation: Though held back many times, they rolled in the dust of the earth, hair loose, stricken with grief, like cows whose calves are slain.
ramayana-6-98-2.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-3.translation: Going out by the northern gate with rakshasas, they entered the dreadful battlefield, searching for their slain husband.
ramayana-6-98-3.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-4.translation: Crying 'Noble husband!' and 'Alas, lord!', they went all over the grim battlefield.
ramayana-6-98-4.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-5.translation: Eyes full of tears, overcome by grief for their husband, they cried out like she-elephants whose leader is slain.
ramayana-6-98-5.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-6.translation: They saw huge, mighty, radiant Ravana lying slain on the ground, like a heap of dark collyrium.
ramayana-6-98-6.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-7.translation: Seeing their husband suddenly, lying in the dust of battle, they fell on his body like cut forest creepers.
ramayana-6-98-7.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-8.translation: One embraced him with great love and wept; one held his feet; one clung to his neck.
ramayana-6-98-8.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-9.translation: One threw up her arms and rolled on the ground; one, seeing the face of the slain, fainted.
ramayana-6-98-9.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-10.translation: One, placing his head in her lap, wept looking at his face, bathing it with tears like a lotus with dew.
ramayana-6-98-10.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-11.translation: So, grieving at the sight of their husband Ravana slain on the ground, they cried out in many ways and lamented again.
ramayana-6-98-11.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-12.translation: 'He who frightened Indra, who frightened Yama, who took the Pushpaka from King Kubera...'
ramayana-6-98-12.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-13.translation: '...who struck great fear into gandharvas, sages and great gods: he lies slain in battle.'
ramayana-6-98-13.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-14.translation: 'He who knew no fear from asuras, gods or serpents has met this danger from a human.'
ramayana-6-98-14.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-15.translation: 'He who could not be slain by gods, danavas or rakshasas lies slain in battle by a human on foot.'
ramayana-6-98-15.meaning: Slain by a man on foot.
ramayana-6-98-15.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-16.translation: 'He whom gods, yakshas and asuras could not slay has been brought to death by a mortal, like some weakling.'
ramayana-6-98-16.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Pride and power do not protect one who does wrong.

ramayana-6-98-17.translation: Saying such things in many ways, his wives wept, and, stricken with grief, lamented again and again.
ramayana-6-98-17.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Even in victory, the epic honours the grief of the defeated.

ramayana-6-98-18.translation: 'By not listening to your friends who always spoke for your good, you have brought down these women, us, and yourself together.'
ramayana-6-98-18.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. A teaching: ignoring wise friends brings ruin to all.

ramayana-6-98-19.translation: 'Your dear brother Vibhishana spoke good words, yet in your delusion, seeking your own death, you spoke harshly to him.'
ramayana-6-98-19.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice.

ramayana-6-98-20.translation: 'If you had returned Sita of Mithila to Rama, this terrible, root-destroying disaster would not have befallen us.'
ramayana-6-98-20.meaning: Returning Sita would have saved them all.
ramayana-6-98-20.explanation: Yuddha Kanda, chapter 98: Ravana's wives come to the battlefield and mourn him, recalling how he ignored all good advice. Doing right in time could have prevented all this suffering.
